fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 13"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Scrutinizing Gaze](/Feats.aspx?ID=3291) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Dwarf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=54" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 201

**Access**
You are from Dongun Hold or Alkenstar.

</column>

---

Your family's traditions of defending against Geb's [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) have granted you a sixth sense for detecting spirits, haunts, and other restless dead, no matter their form or the strength of their presence. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) when trying to determine if a creature is possessed or under the influence of an effect that would make them [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6), a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks made to see through disguises worn by undead, and a +2 circumstance bonus when using the Seek action to find [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) or undead within 30 feet of you.

 If you aren't using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action or searching, the GM automatically rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) check for you to notice haunts or undead within 30 feet anyway. This check doesn't gain the usual +2 circumstance bonus, and instead takes a –2 circumstance penalty.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sculpt Shadows](/Feats.aspx?ID=2511) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Fetchling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=300" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Shadow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=143" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 87

</column>

---

You coax nearby shadows into the shape of a simple weapon or a simple tool or item, using a tiny piece of your shadow to make it solid; in doing so, you lose 1 Hit Point. You can create only level-0 common, non-consumable [weapons](/Weapons.aspx), or [adventuring gear](/Equipment.aspx?Category=1) with no intricate parts, written text, or other complicated components. The item lasts until used for a single activity, until you Sculpt Shadows again, or for 1 minute, whichever comes first. Once the duration expires, the object dissipates, and you regain the lost Hit Point unless the item was [Broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2) or Destroyed. As the object holds a tiny sliver of your shadow, you can't recover the lost Hit Point until after the object dissipates.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Scurry!](/Feats.aspx?ID=5310) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Awakened Animal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=787" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 26

**Prerequisites**
Tiny size

**Trigger**
You roll initiative.

</column>

---

Your instincts to move to safety are strong. You Stride; you must end your movement in a location where you have cover from at least one enemy you can see, and you can't take this action if it's impossible for you to do so. You can [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sea Glass Guardians](/Feats.aspx?ID=4277) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 33

</column>

---

Eerily beautiful elemental water beings race around you, eager to protect and heal you and your allies. Their forms vary and might include eels formed of undulating water or ice crystals whirling in the shape of a jellyfish. The guardians flow around combatants and don't occupy a space. They attempt to intercept all dangers, granting you and your allies within your kinetic aura a +1 status bonus to AC and saving throws.

 If any creature affected is critically hit or critically fails at a saving throw against an attack, effect from an enemy, or hazard and remains above 0 HP, the guardians reach out to heal that creature. The creature regains 4d8+8 Hit Points, and the impulse ends. If the creature is in water, the healing dice are d10s instead of d8s.

---
**Level (+3)** The healing increases by 1d8+4.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Seal of the Golden Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=7102) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 117

**Archetype** [Familiar Sage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=279)

**Prerequisites**
[Familiar Sage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7095); [Golden Dragon's Bounty](/Feats.aspx?ID=7100)

**Trigger**
You would take [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage.

**Requirements**
Your familiar has the resistance ability and is adjacent to you.

</column>

---

Your familiar coils around you, protecting you with its magical resistance. You gain the benefits of your familiar’s [resistance](/Familiars.aspx?ID=122) ability until the start of your next turn. If your familiar has any upgrades to this ability, such as [major resistance](/Familiars.aspx?ID=117), you gain them as well. Once per day, if your familiar’s resistance is a different damage type, your familiar’s resistance ability changes to the appropriate type. If you already have resistance of the same type, choose the higher of the two.

<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />

</traits>

---

They told you there was no way that explosions could heal people, but they were fools… Fools who didn't understand your brilliance! You create a minor explosion from your innovation, altering the combustion to cauterize wounds using vaporized medicinal herbs. You or a living creature adjacent to you regains 1d10 Hit Points. In addition, the creature you heal can attempt an immediate flat check to recover from a single source of [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), with the DC reduction from appropriate assistance.

 At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, increase the healing by 1d10.

**Special** If your innovation is a [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109), it can take this action rather than you, though because it's not a living creature, it can't use the ability on itself.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[Seat of Power](/Feats.aspx?ID=7326) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 112

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

**Prerequisites**
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320)

</column>

---

Your sheer determination has created a demiplane that houses a grand residence which will serve as the heart of your planned realm. You determine the appearance of this seat of power, such as a duskwood longhouse, a crumbling stone castle, an ice tower, or a pagoda constructed from the solidified souls of the damned. You can enter your realm using the Enter Seat of Power activity. You and any creatures you choose gain three times as many Hit Points when [resting](/Rules.aspx?ID=2601) within your seat of power. Once per day while within your seat of power, you can cast [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) as a 4th-rank innate [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell or [_sound body_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1679) as a 4th-rank innate divine spell. You can target only yourself with these spells. 

**Enter Seat of Power** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [exploration](/Skills.aspx?ID=23), [mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835)) **Effect** You focus your mind on your seat of power, then tap into this connection to transport yourself to its demiplane. This process takes 10 minutes. You can bring up to 10 willing creatures with you when you Enter Seat of Power; these creatures must remain within 30 feet of you for the duration of the activity.

 You can remain in your seat of power for as long as you desire. Any creature that you bring to your seat of power in this way (including you) can depart the demiplane as a three-action activity that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait. They return to the location they were in when they Entered your Seat of Power, or the nearest unoccupied space if that location is occupied.

fields.text: Feat 18 Second Chance Spell Enchantment Wizard Source Advanced Player's Guide pg. 143 When your target proves resilient to your magical deceptions, you can try them again on someone else. When you cast an enchantment spell that targets one creature and that creature critically succeeds at its Will save, you can Cast the Spell again before the end of your next turn on a different creature without expending an additional spell slot. The second casting doesn't grant you any benefits that you would normally gain for Casting a Spell from a spell slot.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 198

**Archetype** [Viking](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=81)

**Prerequisites**
[Viking Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2094)

**Trigger**
Your [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) causes your shield to break or be destroyed.

</column>

---

You're used to your shield breaking in the middle of battle, and you're prepared to use a backup or any convenient nearby object to defend yourself. You can Interact to draw a shield on your person or an unattended shield within your reach. If there is an object within your reach that could serve as an improvised shield—for example, a table or chair— you can Interact to draw it with this feat. The GM determines if something can be used as an improvised shield. Your new shield isn't raised until you use the [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98) action, as normal.

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 82 **Archetype** [Timewracked](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=340) **Prerequisites** [Timewracked Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8166) --- You peer into the next several seconds to watch the potential timelines around a nearby creature unfold. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323), then make a check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) at mythic proficiency about a creature you can see. This check gains the following additional effects. **Critical Success** You learn all the actions the creature will take on its next turn (or in the first round of combat if combat hasn’t begun), such as “Stride toward Seelah” or “Cast _shield_.” These actions are locked in and the creature must attempt them, even if the situation changes, though it need not perform the actions in the order stated. For instance, if the creature locked in the actions “Stride toward Seelah,” “Make a longsword Strike against Seelah,” and “Raise a shield,” and Seelah spent her turn moving adjacent to the creature, the creature can make the longsword Strike as its first action if it wishes. If the creature is unable to fulfill an action it committed to, it loses that action as it reels from a temporal paradox. If the situation changes drastically (perhaps Seelah becomes invisible and the creature is unaware where Seelah is), the GM determines what happens.
**Success** You gain one additional piece of information about the creature, as if you had critically succeeded at the [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Press" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=133" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=682" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 162

**Archetype** [Avenger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=282) (Level 14)

**Requirements**
You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand

</column>

---

You read your prey’s movements and transform them into openings, so failures with one weapon set up glancing blows with the other. Make a melee Strike with one of the required weapons against your hunted prey. The Strike gains the following failure effect. 

**Failure** You deal the damage the other required weapon would have dealt on a hit, excluding all damage dice. (This removes dice from weapon runes, spells, and special abilities, not just weapon damage dice.)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=735" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 204

</column>

---

You divert some of your spell’s energy into an unstable runic array. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that deals damage, has no duration, and affects an area, a glowing magic circle appears in a 5-foot burst within that area. At the beginning of your next turn, the circle detonates, dealing 1d6 force damage per rank of the spell to all creatures within the circle, with a basic Reflex save against your spell DC. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the circle deals this type of damage instead (or one type of your choice if the spell could deal multiple types of damage).

---

You have discovered and found favor with the cult within the church of Kabriri known as the Secret Eaters. You have maggots that writhe under your skin with the power to wriggle out from between your teeth, glean secrets from those you devour, and whisper them telepathically into your mind. Once per hour when you [Consume Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504), you can select a single Intelligence-, Wisdom-, or Charisma-based skill whose secrets you wish to uncover. You become subject to the effects of [_corpse communion_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=94) as if you had critically succeeded at casting the ritual: you learn a significant piece of lore, a forgotten secret, or some other tantalizing nugget of knowledge that is of immediate use to you.

<title level="2">Secret Eater leads to...</title>
[Bodysnatcher](/Feats.aspx?ID=3892), [Breath of Hungry Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3894), [Graveshift](/Feats.aspx?ID=3893), [Wrath of the First Ghoul](/Feats.aspx?ID=3895)

>
[Secret Speech](/Feats.aspx?ID=925) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 73

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

Choose a secret society (such as the Lacunafex or the Bellflower Network). You’ve learned that society’s secret cant or jargon, enabling you to share hidden messages when signing or speaking with others who’ve also learned it. If an observer succeeds at a Perception check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC when you do this, they realize you are passing a message but fail to discern its content, unless they subsequently succeed at a Society check against your Deception DC. On a critical success, they learn not only the message, but also who you’re passing the message to.

**Special** You can take this feat multiple times. You learn the secret speech of a different society each time.

<title level="2">Lacunafex Lore</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 72

If the PCs earn Mialari Docur's trust and prove their worth by defeating the Scarlet Triad, she rewards them by granting them access to several feats and spells she and her students have developed over the years.

**Related Feats**: [Different Worlds](/Feats.aspx?ID=923), [Reveal Machinations](/Feats.aspx?ID=924), [Silver's Refrain](/Feats.aspx?ID=926), [Tweak Appearances](/Feats.aspx?ID=927)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[Shadow Reservoir](/Feats.aspx?ID=3013)

</column>

---

Your shadow's voice grows ever clearer; it whispers secrets of true power to you and shields your flesh from harm. Your shadow reservoir gains an additional spell 1 level below the highest level spell you can cast, in addition to the spells it already contains for all the levels below that. 

In addition, the tattoos generated by casting shadow spells protect your body against harmful energies. You gain [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) resistance equal to the highest level of spell you can cast from spell slots; if you have [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42) (or are otherwise harmed by [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128) damage and not negative damage), you instead gain positive resistance in the same amount.

As your prowess with weapons increases, so does the ferocity of magic you channel through those weapons. When you use  [Bespell Strikes](/Feats.aspx?ID=5028), you gain access to the critical specialization effect of the chosen weapon or unarmed attacks used with Bespell Strikes. If you critically hit with an attack modified by Bespell Strikes, you deal an additional 1d8 damage of the same type as the extra damage from Bespell Strikes; this damage is added after all other calculations and is not multiplied as part of the critical hit.

[Seek the Hidden Glyphs](/Feats.aspx?ID=9174) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 48

</column>

---

You are well-versed in the use of magical runes in traps and hazards. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=3303) checks to find magical traps. Even if you aren’t [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630), you get a check to find magical traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap. As long as you are holding or wearing an [artisan’s toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2703), you can use [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) instead of [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) to disable a magical trap, treating your proficiency in Crafting as your proficiency in Thievery for requirements.

In addition, if you trigger a trap by critically failing a check to [Disable](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411) it, you can [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) on yourself as a reaction, gaining the benefits of the rune before the trap affects you.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #164: Hands of the Devil](/Sources.aspx?ID=75) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Eldritch Researcher](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=89)

**Prerequisites**
[Eldritch Researcher Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2658)

</column>

---

Your devotion to discovering and hoarding abstruse truths borders on the fanatical, and you can bring this devotion to bear. You gain the cleric's [Domain Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=265) feat but must select [knowledge](/Domains.aspx?ID=17), [secrecy](/Domains.aspx?ID=28), or [truth](/Domains.aspx?ID=32) as your domain. You cast that domain's domain spell as a focus spell of the same tradition as your cantrip from Eldritch Researcher Dedication, and you [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) by contemplating abstruse mysteries rather than praying to a god. When an ability would manifest a divine symbol—such as the [_word of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=471) focus spell—it instead manifests as a strange shape unique to you that seems to defy geometry.

**Special** You can take this feat up to three times, selecting a different domain each time.

[Seneschal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7249) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 62

**Archetype** [Seneschal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=284)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Seneschal Witch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7247)

</column>

---

You can channel even complex spells through your connection to your charge. If your next action is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) and your charge is within 30 feet, you can have the spell originate from your charge instead. That creature can use their reaction to roughly complete the spell’s incantation, which gives the spell the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait for you (but not for them) as the manifestation appears solely around your charge.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Seneschal Witch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7247) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Class" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=397" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 62

**Archetype** [Seneschal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=284)

**Prerequisites**
Seneschal Witch

</column>

---

As you work to understand the connection with your missing patron, it’s increasingly easy to form bonds with those around you. Raw magical energy spills easily through the connection but, without a patron’s control, it sometimes resists your demands for it to form proper spells.

You gain the [Witch’s Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=5003) feat, but can’t choose your [familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=5024) or another creature with the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait as a charge. When you [cast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) or [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) [_manifest will_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2147), as long as your charge is within 30 feet, you can choose to center the spell’s [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) on your charge instead of yourself.

<title level="2">Seneschal Witch Dedication leads to...</title>
[Multifaceted Will](/Feats.aspx?ID=7250), [Patron Reborn](/Feats.aspx?ID=7255), [Patron's Glamour](/Feats.aspx?ID=7248), [Patron's Whisper](/Feats.aspx?ID=7253), [Seneschal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7249), [Spiritual Secret](/Feats.aspx?ID=7251), [Unstable Patronage](/Feats.aspx?ID=7254), [Watcher on the Wall](/Feats.aspx?ID=7252)

**Source** [Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace](/Sources.aspx?ID=45) pg. 79 **Archetype** [Edgewatch Detective](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=85) **Prerequisites** [Edgewatch Detective Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2193) --- You read the body language of an intelligent creature within 30 feet and pick up on subtle cues to detect its general propensity for good or evil and law or chaos. The GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) Perception check, comparing the result against the target's [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC. **Critical Success** You ascertain the target's alignment.
**Success** You ascertain the target's alignment, but only along one axis (your choice of either the good-evil axis or the lawful-chaotic axis).
**Failure** You do not learn the target's alignment.
**Critical Failure** You incorrectly ascertain the target's alignment, misidentifying their alignment along either one axis or both (GM's choice).

    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"

>
[Sense Allies](/Feats.aspx?ID=1437) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=90" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 47

</column>

---

Like many humans raised in a close-knit community, you have always been strongly attuned to the presence of others. Willing allies that you are aware of within 60 feet that would otherwise be [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by you are instead [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from you. The flat check for you to target willing allies within 60 feet that are hidden from you is 5 instead of 11.

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 84 **Archetype** [Hellknight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=25) **Prerequisites** [Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1078) --- You sense chaos as an unsettling feeling of nervous energy. When in the presence of an aura of chaos that is powerful or overwhelming, you eventually detect the aura, though you might not do so instantly and you can’t pinpoint the location. This is a vague sense, similar to humans’ sense of smell. A chaotic creature using a disguise or otherwise trying to hide its presence attempts a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check against your Perception DC to hide its aura from you. If the creature succeeds at its Deception check, it is temporarily immune to your Sense Chaos for 1 day. Alignment Aura The strength of an alignment aura depends on the level of the creature, item, or spell. The auras of undead, clerics and other divine spellcasters with a patron deity, and creatures from the Outer Sphere are one step stronger than normal (faint instead of none, for example). ## Alignment Aura
**Creature or Item Level****Spell or Effect Level****Aura Strength**
0-5—None
6-100-3Faint
11-154-7Moderate
16-208-9Powerful
21+10Overwhelming

You sense evil as a queasy or foreboding feeling. You detect unholy creatures as a [vague sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=2408), similar to humans’ sense of smell. An unholy creature using a disguise or otherwise trying to hide its presence attempts a Deception check against your Perception DC to hide its unholiness from you. If the creature succeeds at its Deception check, it is then temporarily immune to your Sense Evil for 1 day.

[Sense Iniquity](/Feats.aspx?ID=8823) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 26

**Archetype** [Hellknight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=372)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8812)

</column>

---

Your Hellknight training gives you the ability to focus your senses and root out those who would attempt to deceive or hide from you. For 1 minute, you gain a +2 status bonus to your Perception DC against attempts to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387), [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) you, or [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) to you. During this time, if you [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) to locate a [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) creature or to see through a creature's [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) attempt, you gain a +2 status bonus to the Perception check.

During this time, if you Seek to locate a hidden creature or to see through a creature's Impersonate attempt, you gain a +2 status bonus to the Perception check.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #201: Pactbreaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=241) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Verduran Shadow](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=312)

**Prerequisites**
[Verduran Shadow Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7606); Master in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49)

**Trigger**
A creature targets you with an [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540) and you can see the attacker.

</column>

---

You sense how an incoming attack moves through ambient primal energy, predicting how best to dodge. The triggering attack targets your [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) DC instead of your AC. Though this allows you to avoid taking penalties to your AC, it doesn’t remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with sneak attack would still deal extra damage to you for being [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), even though you wouldn’t take the –2 circumstance penalty when defending against the attack.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=818" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=682" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 162, [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 112

**Archetypes** [Shadowdancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=77) (Level 16), [Exorcist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171) (Level 16), [Steel Falcon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=374) (Level 16), [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381) (Level 16)

**Trigger**
You fail a check to Seek

</column>

---

When you look for foes, you can catch even the slightest cues, such as their minute movements or the shifting of air currents on your skin. Even though you failed at the triggering check, you automatically sense any undetected creatures in the area where you’re Seeking, making them merely hidden to you.

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sense Unholiness](/Feats.aspx?ID=7521) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 277

**Archetype** [Exorcist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171) (Level 14)

**Prerequisites**
[[Champion](/Classes.aspx?ID=58)] [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517)

</column>

---

You sense the truly wicked as a queasy or foreboding feeling. You can sense the presence of creatures with the unholy trait within 120 feet. This functions as a vague sense, similar to humans’ sense of smell. An unholy creature using a disguise or otherwise trying to hide its presence attempts a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check against your [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=3303) DC to hide its sanctification from you. If the creature succeeds at its Deception check, it is then temporarily immune to your Sense Unholiness for 1 day.

>
[Sentinel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2062) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 191

**Archetype** [Sentinel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=76)

</column>

---

You have trained carefully to maximize the protective qualities of your armor. You become trained in light armor and medium armor. If you already were trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in heavy armor as well. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you are at least 13th level and you have a class feature that grants you expert proficiency in unarmored defense, you also become an expert in the armor types granted to you by this feat.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the sentinel archetype.

<title level="2">Sentinel Dedication leads to...</title>
[Armor Specialist](/Feats.aspx?ID=2064), [Armored Rebuff](/Feats.aspx?ID=2065), [Mighty Bulwark](/Feats.aspx?ID=2066), [Steel Skin](/Feats.aspx?ID=2063)

You repurpose the negative energy that flows through your minions at a moment's notice. Instantly destroy one undead minion within 60 feet that is permanently under your control. The spell's level must be half the destroyed minion's level or lower and the spell can't have a duration.

Your people's ancient and storied rivalry with [garudas](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1162) led you to develop special techniques against flying foes. Make a melee Strike against a flying creature up to one size larger than you; if you hit, you use your neck or coils to smash the creature into the ground. In addition to the normal effects of your Strike, the creature moves to the nearest unoccupied ground space adjacent to you and can't [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94), [_levitate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=170), or otherwise leave the ground for 1 round. On a critical hit, it can't Fly, levitate, or otherwise leave the ground for 1 minute.

Many traditions hold the number seven as significant. By exchanging pieces of a seven-part set of esoterica, you create a magical web by which your allies can affect each other at a distance. When you use Paired Link during your daily preparations, you can exchange linking esoterica with up to six willing allies, keeping one piece for yourself. In addition to the normal effects of Paired Link, if a linked ally casts a spell with a range of touch, they can target linked allies within 30 feet with that spell.

You are wielding a weapon that deals slashing damage or have an unarmed Strike that deals slashing damage.

---

You destroy the space between you and your targets, allowing you to strike with your melee weapons at great range. Make a melee Strike with the required weapon or unarmed attack. The attack gains an 80-foot [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) for this Strike.

 After the Strike, regardless of whether it succeeded, the world rushes to fill the space you destroyed, bringing you and the target adjacent to each other. You can choose to teleport to the closest space adjacent to the target or to attempt to teleport the target adjacent to you. If you choose the target, they can negate the teleportation if they succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC.

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 75

**Prerequisites**
[Inherit the Dreaming Heirloom](/Feats.aspx?ID=6951)

</column>

---

As you whisper to your pusaka, it attempts to cut away an enemy’s shadow, leaving them in an eternal sleep. Your pusaka gains the following Activation. 

**Activate—Cut the Shadow** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your pusaka becomes a [kris](/Weapons.aspx?ID=264) made of darkness and drives itself into an adjacent enemy’s shadow. That enemy takes 80 mental damage with a basic Fortitude save against your spell DC or class DC, whichever is higher. If this reduces the creature to 0 Hit Points, the target doesn’t die, but its shadow is severed from its body, becoming a [shadow spawn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3186) that attempts to flee from the target’s body. As long as the shadow spawn exists, the target remains in a dreamless slumber; if destroyed, the target regains its shadow and awakens (if its body was kept properly while [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95)).

</title>

<traits>

---

As the gap between your intention and your words becomes almost nothing, you find that you don't need to consciously draw the diacritic marks that would embellish or modify your runes. As you draw a rune, it continues to grow outward like a living thing, applying the exact accent or stress mark you intended for it to have. Whenever you etch or [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264), you can choose to also apply one [diacritic](/Traits.aspx?ID=948) rune you know to it as part of the same action.

---

You gain the ability to fuse and play with shadows by using focus spells specific to shadowdancers. You learn a shadowdancer focus spell of your choice: [_dance of darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=662) or [_shadow jump_](/Spells.aspx?ID=664). If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) by meditating within an area of dim light or darkness. The rules for focus spells appear [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=276).

Shadowdancer focus spells are occult spells. You become trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs, and your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

<traits>

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

You have learned special tricks that help you follow individuals without them noticing you. When you attempt a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check to [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=511) while following a specific target, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their Perception DC. If you have master proficiency in Stealth, the penalty is –3 or –4 if you're legendary. If you start an encounter with the target while shadowing them, the target takes this penalty to their initiative roll and to their Perception DC to determine if they notice you, as normal for [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63).

Thousands of years ago, your ancestors made a pact with [Zon-Kuthon](/Deities.aspx?ID=20). He has not forgotten, even if you might wish he had. You can take 1 damage to mix blood and shadows to cast 5th-level [_creation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=54) as an innate divine spell. If the object encounters bright light, the spell ends and the object dissolves into shadows.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shadow Reservoir](/Feats.aspx?ID=3013) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 226

**Archetype** [Shadowcaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=101)

**Prerequisites**
ability to cast spells from spell slots; [Shadowcaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3009)

</column>

---

Your own shadow speaks to you, providing knowledge of spells and a reservoir of magical power. Your shadow reservoir contains a single spell of each spell level at least 2 levels lower than the highest-level spell you can cast from your spell slots. This spell must come from your spell list, you must have access to it, and it must require a spell attack roll or a saving throw. These spells don't need to be prepared and aren't in your repertoire.

 Regardless of the way in which you cast spells, you can spontaneously cast a spell from your shadow reservoir by using one of your spell slots of the same level. If you're a prepared spellcaster, you lose the spell you prepared in that slot.

 Spells cast from your shadow reservoir gain the [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=143) trait, and affected creatures might be able to [disbelieve](/Rules.aspx?ID=267) them. If the spell requires an attack roll, use the higher of the target's AC or their Will DC. If the spell requires a saving throw, the target uses their Will saving throw or the spell's normal saving throw, whichever is higher. Each time a creature fails its saving throw against a spell cast from your reservoir, you gain a small tattoo inked on your flesh out of pure shadowstuff.

 If you have more than one source of spells you can cast with spell slots, such as if you're a spellcaster with a multiclass archetype, choose one source of spells for your shadow reservoir.

[Secrets of Shadow](/Feats.aspx?ID=3014)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Halfling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=87" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 46

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

**Trigger**
You successfully use [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) and become [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from all your current foes, or use Stealth to [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) and become [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) to all your current foes.

</column>

---

With a powerful talent for misdirection, you slip from your adversaries' notice so thoroughly you appear to be somewhere else. You become [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) for 1 minute or until you take a hostile action, whichever comes first. Choose a location within 10 feet of you. Until your invisibility ends, you appear to be hidden in that location to anyone trying to find you. If the searcher gets clear evidence that you're not there, they no longer think you're hidden there, but they don't discover your actual location.

**Prerequisites**
[Shadowcaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3009)

</column>

---

You attach a piece of your shadow to a spell to cloud the senses and cause mischief. If the next action you take is to Cast a Spell that has the [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=143) trait, choose one creature affected by the spell. This creature either gains a +2 status bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) or takes a –2 status penalty to Perception (your choice). This lasts for 1 round. This choice and the effect occur after resolving any checks for the spell's initial effects. If the chosen creature is your enemy, it's affected only if your spell attack roll succeeded or if it failed its saving throw.

 The effects of Shadow Spell end if you use Shadow Spell again.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 226

**Archetype** [Shadowcaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=101)

**Prerequisites**
ability to cast spells

</column>

---

You've sacrificed a piece of your spirit, allowing the powers of shadow into your being and changing the nature of your magic. You can no longer cast spells that have the [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) trait; if an ability, such as a class feature or ancestry feat, would automatically grant you a light spell, such as the [Domain Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=265) feat granting you the [_dazzling flash_](/Spells.aspx?ID=412) spell, you don't gain that spell.

 You gain the [_cloak of shadow_](/Spells.aspx?ID=407) domain spell. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus spell. This feat grants a focus pool of 1 Focus Point that you can recover using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity. You can Refocus by meditating to siphon power from the [Shadow Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=11) and refill your focus pool. Your domain spells from the shadowcaster archetype are of the same tradition as the spells you used to meet the shadowcaster archetype's prerequisites.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the shadowcaster archetype.

<title level="2">Shadowcaster Dedication leads to...</title>
[Disciple of Shade](/Feats.aspx?ID=3011), [Shadow Reservoir](/Feats.aspx?ID=3013), [Shadow Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=3012), [Shadow Spells](/Feats.aspx?ID=3010), [Unending Emptiness](/Feats.aspx?ID=3015)

Master in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15); Expert in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

You dedicate yourself to the shadows. Your coloring becomes gray and gloomy, your senses adjust to the darkness, and you can sneak through darkness with ease. You gain [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12). You also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks when you are within dim light or darkness.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the shadowdancer archetype.

<title level="2">Shadowdancer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Shadow Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=2069), [Shadow Master](/Feats.aspx?ID=2073), [Shadow Sneak Attack](/Feats.aspx?ID=2068)

---

You charge into the fray on horseback, and those that lurk in the shadows will feel your wrath. You [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) to have your mount Stride up to double its Speed. You can make a melee Strike at up to two enemies that are within your reach at any point during your mount's movement. Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after you've made both of them.

 Each Strike that hits a creature in [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2401) or darkness deals an additional 3d6 damage of the same type as the Strike. This additional damage increases to 4d6 at 15th level and to 5d6 at 18th level.

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Misfortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=654" />
<trait label="Wandering" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=843" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 26

**Trigger**
You would be detected by an enemy [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) you, or an enemy would succeed at a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) check against a spell making you [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96).

**Requirements**
Your attuned apparition grants Hunting [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) or Underworld Lore as one of its apparition skills.

</column>

---

Your apparition possesses a furtive and elusive nature that can influence and blend with your spiritual energy to form a protective and nearly impenetrable shroud of nondetection around you. The enemy must reroll the triggering check and take the lower result.

>

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 69

**Archetype** [Knight Reclaimant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=28)

**Prerequisites**
[Knight Reclaimant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1097)

</column>

---

You gain the [_shall not falter, shall not rout_](/Spells.aspx?ID=817) focus spell. If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can regain using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity to recite the Crimson Oath and meditate on its teachings. If you already have a focus pool, increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1. Your knight reclaimant focus spells are divine spells; when you gain this feat, you become trained in divine spell attacks and spell DCs and your spellcasting ability is Charisma.

<title level="2">Knights in Training</title>

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 68

The following feats represent benefits of training from the Iomedars (Kalabrynne for knight vigilant, Clarethe for knight reclaimant, either for Lastwall sentry).

**Related Feats**: [Rescuer's Press](/Feats.aspx?ID=2167), [Vigil's Walls Rise Anew!](/Feats.aspx?ID=2169)

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 61

**Archetype** [Zombie](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=182)

**Prerequisites**

---

You may be slower than you were in life, but your pace is unfaltering. Stride twice, or three times if you spent 3 actions to Shamble. During this movement, you ignore difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain.

 You can choose to ignore all circumstance and status penalties to your Speed when you Shamble. If you do, you must succeed at a DC 6 flat check when you finish Shambling or your body deteriorates.

[Shame the Sin](/Feats.aspx?ID=7657) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 80

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Trigger**
You critically hit a [demon](/Traits.aspx?ID=573) with a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

</column>

---

Your conviction against the sins that all demons grow from is so strong that you can force a demon to suffer from its sins when you strike a sound blow against them. In addition to doing the normal damage for your critical hit, the demon also suffers the effects of its special [vulnerability](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312). If the demon has no special vulnerability, it instead takes an additional 1d6 [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) damage. This increases to 2d6 mental damage at 13th level and to 3d6 mental damage at 17th level.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 262

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

You can downplay the consequences or outrageousness of your requests using sheer brazenness and charm. When you Request something, you reduce any DC increases for making an outrageous request by 2, and if you roll a critical failure for your Request, you get a failure instead. While this means you can never cause your target to reduce their attitude toward you by making a Request, they eventually tire of requests, even though they still have a positive attitude toward you.

Once per day, you can cast 7th-level [_dragon form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=88) as an innate arcane spell, transforming into a [cloud dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=176). The spell automatically heightens to 8th level if you're 16th level and 9th level if you're 18th level. On a critical hit with an unarmed Strike gained from _dragon form_, you recharge the spell's breath weapon immediately. While in this form, you gain the following cloud dragon–specific abilities:
  • **Cloud** cloud walk (you can walk on clouds or fog); **Melee** jaws, **Damage** 2d10 piercing plus 1d12 electricity; **Melee** claw ([agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 3d10 slashing; **Melee** tail ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10 bludgeoning; **Melee** horn ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8 piercing; breath weapon 30-foot cone, 6d12 electricity.
**Special** You can use this feat in place of [Shape of the Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=1947) to fulfill feat requirements. Bloodsalt Dragon Disciple Feats **Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 79 The following archetype feats are for the dragon disciple archetype. You must take the Dragon Disciple Dedication feat before selecting any of these feats, and you must select cloud dragon (which is associated with the electricity energy type) as the type of dragon you've studied. The feats below are dragon disciple archetype feats. By studying the ruins (see the AP for full details), you gain access to the dragon disciple archetype and to these feats If you have the [draconic sorcerer](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=5) bloodline, you must choose cloud dragon as your dragon type. This choice affects the [_dragon breath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=499) and [_dragon claws_](/Spells.aspx?ID=500) bloodline spells and several of the feats below. **Related Feats**: [Cloud Walk](/Feats.aspx?ID=3406), [Deflecting Cloud](/Feats.aspx?ID=3408), [Mighty Wings](/Feats.aspx?ID=3409)

    right="Feat 12"

>
[Shaped Contaminant](/Feats.aspx?ID=1153) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #149: Against the Scarlet Triad](/Sources.aspx?ID=14) pg. 78

</column>

---

Through a combination of careful manipulation and precise breath control, you can deploy inhaled toxins precisely. When you activate an [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) poison, you can cause it to fill a 20-foot line that’s 5 feet tall rather than a 10-foot cube. You gain a +3 status bonus to saving throws against inhaled poisons that you activate.

<title level="2">Katapesh Poisoners</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #149: Against the Scarlet Triad](/Sources.aspx?ID=14) pg. 78

Famous not only for its pesh cash crop and the host of medicinal plants that grow naturally in the nearby desert, but also for the consistent demand for efficient toxins, Katapesh has developed its own specialized poisons and toxic techniques. The city's infamous Poison Maker's Guild is the source of many of these concoctions as well as secret techniques for using them, though unscrupulous Katapeshi bodyguards, thieves, and assassins all know at least one poison recipe or a unique means of inflicting such toxins.

**Related Feats**: [Deadly Poison Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=1151), [Pesh Skin](/Feats.aspx?ID=1152)

<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 30

</column>

---

Jagged metal shards form in the air and lash out from you. You choose shards or spines, which changes the area, damage type, and critical failure effect. Each creature in the area attempts a basic Reflex save against your class DC. Shards deal 1d6 slashing damage in a 15-foot cone, and a creature that critically fails takes 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Spines deal 1d6 piercing damage in a 30-foot line, and a creature that critically fails is [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) until the start of your next turn.

---
**Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d6.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227), mortal weakness

**Requirements**
You are Exploiting a creature's Vulnerability using mortal weakness.

</column>

---

You select an object from your esoterica that has great personal value to you, such as a locket or treasured ring, and you grant it to an ally, establishing a personal link that allows your ally to affect an enemy as if they were you. The ally's Strikes apply the weakness from your mortal weakness the same way your Strikes do. This benefit ends when your Exploit Vulnerability ends or you Share Weakness again.

<title level="2">Share Weakness leads to...</title>
[Ubiquitous Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=3733)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=19" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 114

**Prerequisites**
[Courageous Assault](/Feats.aspx?ID=1649)

</column>

---

In the triumph of battle, you can share the glory with another ally. When the ally you chose for [Courageous Assault](/Feats.aspx?ID=1649) critically succeeds at the Strike granted by that action, another ally affected by your [_inspire courage_](/Spells.aspx?ID=386) composition spell can immediately use a reaction to make a melee Strike. Since the second ally wasn't the ally you chose for Courageous Assault, this effect doesn't continue to a third ally, even if the second ally also critically succeeds at their Strike.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

**Prerequisites**
[focus pool](/Rules.aspx?ID=2228)

</column>

---

Your magical expertise allows you to perform a metaphorical sleight of hand to manifest a Focus Point. Choose a willing ally within 30 feet who also has a [focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) pool. The target gains 1 temporary Focus Point until the start of your next turn, at which time it’s lost, even if not spent. This temporary Focus Point is separate from the Focus Points in their focus pool, allowing them to have it even if they’re at their pool’s maximum. The creature then becomes temporarily immune to Shared Focus until their next daily preparations.

---

You are evidence that it’s lucky to travel with a halfling. You can use Halfling Luck when an ally within 30 feet fails a skill check or a saving throw to allow the ally to reroll the triggering check instead of you rerolling your own failed check. As usual, your ally must use the new result, even if it’s worse than their first roll. If you have [Guiding Luck](/Feats.aspx?ID=62), you can’t use Guiding Luck’s effect that applies to attack rolls and Perception checks to use Shared Luck to benefit an ally.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shared Mind, Shared Heart](/Feats.aspx?ID=7957) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 63

**Archetype** [Iridian Choirmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=328)

**Prerequisites**
[Iridian Choirmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7943)

</column>

---

Your thoughts and dreams are your student's thoughts and dreams, and vice versa. You develop a permanent mental  connection, allowing you to communicate telepathically as long as you're on the same plane. When one of you fails a save against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, the other can choose to take the results of the failed save instead. If both of you are targeted by the same mental effect requiring a saving throw, you and your student take the better of each of your die rolls for the save. You each still add your own save modifier to the die result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect.

You've experimented enough on your teammates to transfer a substantial number of powered-up gizmos to them, enabling one of your allies to benefit from the full effects and duration of your [Overdrive](/Actions.aspx?ID=901). As long as you’re wearing your clothing, you gain a +1 item bonus to unarmed attack rolls, [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks, and Reflex saves and DCs to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296), [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313), or avoid falling [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Shatter Space](/Feats.aspx?ID=3687) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Amp" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=425" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 28

</column>

---

The sheer power of your magic fractures reality. Use this amp in place of a psi cantrip's normal amp entry. The cantrip must be one that takes 2 or more actions to cast.

---
**Amp** You or one target of the spell are surrounded by a spiral of torn space. This is an aura, and you choose the radius of the emanation, up to 20 feet. A creature that starts its turn in the aura or enters the aura during its turn takes 1d6 slashing damage for every level of the amped psi cantrip, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your spell DC. If the creature critically fails, the torn space throws it off balance and it falls prone. The aura lasts until the beginning of your next turn. You can choose whether the aura affects the creature emitting it.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Shattered Sacrament](/Feats.aspx?ID=7742) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Claws of the Tyrant](/Sources.aspx?ID=266) pg. 110

**Archetype** [Halcyon Speaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=30)

**Prerequisites**
[Halcyon Speaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1115); [Cascade Bearer's Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=1110)

</column>

---

When Vigil fell to Tar-Baphon’s Radiant Fire, that lost innocence brought you a deeper understanding of what faith means in the context of your own magic. When you cast a halcyon spell, you can choose for it to be a [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell instead of [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) or [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4). You gain a halcyon cantrip and a 1st-rank halcyon spell.

<title level="2">Shattered Sacrament leads to...</title>
[Tripartite Omen](/Feats.aspx?ID=7745)

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shattering Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3194) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 117

**Requirements**
You're wielding a loaded firearm or loaded crossbow and are wearing or holding an alchemical [bomb](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&amp;Subcategory=7).

</column>

---

You fling a bomb into the air and then shoot it with your gun before it falls, raining destruction down over a wide area. If necessary, you Interact to draw the bomb and regrip your weapon. You throw your bomb to the corner of a square within your firearm's first range increment and shoot it with your firearm. All creatures in a 15-foot burst of the bomb take the bomb's normal damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. They don't take any [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) or [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) the bomb would deal normally.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shattering Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7467) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Force" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=610" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 83

**Prerequisites**
[Resurgent Maelstrom Hybrid Study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=9), Spellstrike

**Requirements**
You’re in Arcane Cascade stance and wielding an improvised weapon.

</column>

---

You intentionally channel a rampaging cascade of magic through your weapon, breaking it to deal more damage. Make a Spellstrike against a target with your improvised weapon. If the attack hits, it deals an additional 2d6 force damage as your improvised weapon breaks. If the spell used with the Spellstrike wasn’t a cantrip or focus spell, increase this additional damage by the spell’s rank.

 If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it’s an artifact, cursed item, or other item that’s difficult to break or destroy, it doesn’t break and you don’t deal additional damage.

[Improvised Pummel](/Feats.aspx?ID=2100)

**Trigger**
An improvised weapon that you are wielding becomes broken as a result of a critical success on an Improvised Pummel.

The improvised weapon shatters, destroying it completely but dealing an additional 3d6 piercing damage to the creature you hit with the [Improvised Pummel](/Feats.aspx?ID=2100). This extra damage you apply on the critical hit doesn't double from the critical hit, as normal.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />

<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 31

---

Four plates of pitted metal float around you to intercept attacks. You and allies in your kinetic aura gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC. When any creature with this bonus would take damage from a physical attack, one of the plates reduces the damage by its Hardness of 5. If the damage exceeds the Hardness, that plate is destroyed. You can replenish all destroyed plates as a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.

---
**Level (+2)** The Hardness increases by 1.

You can shed your tail to escape. You cease being grabbed, then Stride without triggering any reactions from the creature that grabbed you. It takes 1 week for your tail to fully grow back. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=52" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 199

**Prerequisites**
[stone order](/DruidicOrders.aspx?ID=6)

**Requirements**
You're standing on ground composed of earth, stone, or a similar material.

</column>

---

You spend 10 minutes communing with spirits of earth and stone, requesting shelter. At the end of this time, the earth rises and opens, forming a small cave or earthen mound 20 feet in diameter and 10 feet high. This cave has the [structure](/Traits.aspx?ID=153) trait and the same restrictions as structures created by magic items. The cave has a single entrance and provides shelter from the elements. The cave remains for 12 hours or until you spend 10 minutes coaxing the earth to close.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />

</column>

---

Animals, plants, and the earth itself rush to protect you from harm, interposing themselves between you and danger. You and your allies in your waking world gain [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2559) from enemies you are aware of until the start of your next turn. The cover is based on the number of actions you spend. If you use one action, it is lesser cover; if you spend two actions, it is standard cover.

The stone around you is your ally, and you have learned to use it to shore up your weaknesses. This works even if you are at the outside corner of the wall.

    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Shield of Stone](/Feats.aspx?ID=8011) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #217: Death Sails a Wine-Dark Sea
](/Sources.aspx?ID=273) pg. 79

**Usage**
imbued into the [_mirrored aegis_](/Ikons.aspx?ID=9)

</column>

---

You stole a [gorgon’s](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=496) gaze and trapped it in your ikon. You’ve learned how to brandish it for your advantage, subduing the rage of the trapped gaze by turning it on your enemies. 

**Transcendence—Brandish the Gorgon’s Gaze** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585), [transcendence](/Traits.aspx?ID=842), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Effect** You Raise your mirrored aegis, though it seems to lose some of its usual luster in favor of the dull sheen of stone. If you [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) a melee attack with the mirrored aegis before the beginning of your next turn, the gorgon’s eyes upon it flash at the triggering creature, who must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC. On a failure, they are [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 minute as their body partially petrifies. Regardless of the outcome, that creature is temporarily immune to this effect for 24 hours.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 115

**Prerequisites**
[divine ally (shield)](/Classes.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

Your shield is a vessel of divine protection. When you’re wielding your chosen shield, it is always raised, even without you using the Raise a Shield action. Your chosen shield doubles its HP and BT, rather than increasing them by half. If it would be destroyed, it vanishes to your deity’s realm instead, where your divine ally repairs it. During your next daily preparations, the shield returns to you fully repaired.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shield Spell Reinforcement](/Feats.aspx?ID=7978) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 68

**Archetype** [War Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=331)

**Prerequisites**
[War Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7976); you can cast the [_shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1671) cantrip

**Requirements**
You are wielding a shield.

</column>

---

You can empower your defensive magic by channeling it through a physical shield. If your next action is to cast the _shield_ cantrip, you use your shield as a locus to cast the spell, raising a magical barrier in the form of a large force projection of your worn shield. You can choose for an adjacent ally to gain the benefits of the _shield_ spell instead of yourself. If the ally would take damage from a physical attack while protected by your shield cantrip, you can use your reaction to [Shield Block](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=75) with the spell on their behalf.

    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shield the Faithful](/Feats.aspx?ID=7534) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Aura" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=206" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Sanctified" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=519" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 280

**Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Mortal Herald Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7528)

</column>

---

You and those closest to you are protected by your deity’s power. For 1 minute, you and all allies within 10 feet of you gain a +1 item bonus to AC and [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 10 to spirit damage. In addition, when a creature adjacent to you hits you with a melee attack, or when a creature touches you or hits you with an unarmed attack, that creature takes 5 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage.

At 20th level, the spirit resistance increases to 15 and the spirit damage increases to 10.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shield Wall](/Feats.aspx?ID=3634) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 84

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

**Trigger**
Your shield is raised and an adjacent ally [Raises a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98).

</column>

---

You use your shield in tandem with an ally's, forming a barricade. Both you and the triggering creature have [standard cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) as long as you remain adjacent to each other and you both have your shields raised; when this is no longer the case, the effect ends. You and your ally can't use this cover to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62), as it's obvious you're standing there holding your shields, but you and your ally can use it to [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=90). Normally, if you and your ally don't move, Shield Wall lasts until the beginning of your next turn, when your shield is no longer raised.

>
[Shield Wallop](/Feats.aspx?ID=7861) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Guardian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=859" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 45

**Requirements**
You are wearing a shield.

</column>

---

Attacks with your shield knock the sense out of your foes. Make a [shield bash](/Weapons.aspx?ID=395), [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=396), or [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=397) Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target is [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 until the start of your next turn (stupefied 2 on a critical hit). If your shield is a [tower shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=20), [fortress shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=7), or another shield that grants a higher circumstance bonus to AC when you [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=2307) behind it, the creature is instead stupefied 2 if you hit and deal damage to it (stupefied 3 on a critical hit).

You can bandage wounds with the same hand you use to hold  your shield. You can use the same hand you are using to wield  a shield to [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399) or use [Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=5125), and you are considered to have a hand free for other uses of Medicine as  long as the only thing you are holding or wielding in that hand is a shield. When you use Battle Medicine on an ally while  wielding a shield, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and Reflex saves that lasts until the start of your next turn or until they are no longer adjacent to you, whichever comes first.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetypes** [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=49) (Level 6), [Viking](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=81) (Level 6), [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=240) (Level 6), [Viking](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=268) (Level 6)

When your shield is up, your enemies' blows can't touch you. When you have your shield raised, you can Stride to move half your Speed without triggering reactions that are triggered by your movement (such as [Attacks of Opportunity](/Actions.aspx?ID=8)). You can use Shielded Stride while [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

</column>

---

During your daily preparations, you can magically fuse a shield into your favorite book, where it appears as an elaborate bookmark. While the two are fused, the book shares the Hardness, Hit Points, and Broken Threshold of the shield, and it can be used to [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) if you have that reaction, with a requirement of “You have Raised the Tome” instead of the usual requirements.

 You can switch the fused item's form from a book to a shield with a book-shaped motif as a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. When the item is in book form, you can read the book and Raise the Tome, and when it's in shield form, you can [Raise the Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98), Activate it, and gain any other benefits or effects the shield normally has (such as a [_spellguard shield's_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=325) bonus to saving throws against magic). The fusion lasts until your next daily preparations.

You can magically fuse a [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12) into your favorite book during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait. The shield appears in the book as an elaborate bookmark. The fusion lasts until you fuse a shield into a new book or the book is out of your possession for 24 hours. While the two are fused, the book shares the Hardness, Hit Points, and Broken Threshold of the shield. The fused item has the shield’s activations and benefits (such as a [_spellguard shield_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2826)’s bonus to saving throws against magic), and it can still be consulted as normal for purposes like [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) and the benefits of [Raise a Tome](/Feats.aspx?ID=2848). If the shield or your spellbook is etched with a [_reinforcing rune_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2811), the fused item gains the rune while they’re fused; if both have the rune, the highest-level rune applies.

fields.text: Feat 14 Shifting Terrain Single Action Archetype Source Secrets of Magic pg. 213 Archetype Geomancer Prerequisites Rough Terrain Stance; Master in Nature Requirements Your terrain attunement matches the terrain you're in and you're in Rough Terrain Stance. You slam your fist into the ground or twirl your arms about to cause the terrain around you to shift and ripple, potentially throwing others off balance. Each creature within your area of difficult terrain from Rough Terrain Stance must attempt a Reflex saving throw against your spell DC with the following effects. After you use this action, you can't use it again for 1d4 rounds. Critical Success The creature is unaffected. Success The creature is clumsy 1 for 1 round. Failure The creature is clumsy 2 for 1 round. Critical Failure The creature is clumsy 2 for 1 round and falls prone.

When you cast _light_, you can modify its target to be 1 melee weapon, either unattended or possessed by you or a willing ally, and modify its duration to be 1 minute. If you do, add the following to its effects: When a creature wielding the weapon critically hits a foe, you can Dismiss the Spell as a reaction, causing the foe to be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shining Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=221) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Oath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=119" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 110

**Prerequisites**
[tenets of good](/Tenets.aspx?ID=1)

</column>

---

You’ve sworn an oath to put the undead to rest. You gain the following edict: “You must end the existence of undead you encounter as long as you have a reasonable chance of success; in the unlikely event you find an undead that isn't unholy, you can try to work out a more peaceful way to help it recover from its undead state rather than destroying it in combat, such as helping it complete its unfinished business and find peace.”

 Your Retributive Strike gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage against an undead, or +6 if you have master proficiency with the weapon you used. Your Glimpse of Redemption’s resistance against damage from an undead is 7 + your level. If you use Liberating Step triggered by an undead, your ally gains a +4 circumstance bonus to checks granted by your Liberating Step, and the ally can Step twice afterward.

 You don’t consider undead to be legitimate authorities, even in nations ruled by undead.

<title level="2">Shining Oath leads to...</title>
[Aura of Life](/Feats.aspx?ID=250)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 73

**Archetype** [Avenging Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=338)

**Prerequisites**
[Avenging Runelord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8139)

</column>

---

Whenever you [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that requires more than one action to cast, the signature Thassilonian runes you trace in the air flicker with light and command attention. They may blaze brightly, leave lingering fog, create discordant noise, or fill the air with an overwhelming scent, such that their presence obfuscates you from onlookers. You gain concealment from enemy creatures until the beginning of your next turn. The DC to [identify](/Rules.aspx?ID=2249) your spells as you cast them is 2 higher than normal.
