    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shore Gift](/Feats.aspx?ID=5354) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Merfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=761" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 38

</column>

---

Using old magic, you slip off your tail like an item of clothing and walk on two feet, resembling a humanoid ancestry, usually [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6) but possibly [elf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=2), [half-elf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=7), or something stranger. You're still recognizably yourself, as the Shore Gift doesn't change your upper body. While transformed, you lose your swim Speed from your ancestry (though you might still have a swim Speed from other sources) but gain a land Speed of 25 feet.

 Using the Shore Gift also counts as creating a disguise when using [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388), and your transformation automatically defeats Perception DCs to determine if you're a normal member of whatever ancestry you appear to be; only creatures actively rolling Perception to examine you might notice the disguise. You can remain in your alternate form indefinitely and can shift back to your merfolk form by using this action again.

<title

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Shorthanded](/Feats.aspx?ID=3224) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 129

**Archetype** [Artillerist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=115)

**Prerequisites**
[Artillerist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3222)

</column>

---

Typically, a [siege weapon](/SiegeWeapons.aspx) is meant to be run by a crew with a very specific minimum number of members designed to ensure that your crew can account for every possible variable and necessity in loading, aiming, and firing the weapon. In a pinch, however, you can operate it with fewer people, provided you know what you're doing. You can operate a siege weapon with fewer than the minimum number of crew, at an increasing penalty. You and your crew take a –2 penalty to checks to [Load](/Rules.aspx?ID=1624), [Aim](/Rules.aspx?ID=1625), [Launch](/Rules.aspx?ID=1626), move, or [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) the weapon for each person below the minimum crew. The maximum number of missing minimum crew members you can handle with this feat is 5. For example, if a siege weapon had a minimum crew size of 8, you would still need a crew of 3, and you would take a –10 penalty when doing so.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Show-Off](/Feats.aspx?ID=4144) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Acrobat](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=236)

**Frequency**
once per minute

**Prerequisites**
[Acrobat Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1873)

**Access**
Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

**Trigger**
You succeed at an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) or [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check deemed suitably challenging and meaningful by the GM.

</column>

---

As is the tradition with many Firebrands, you call your shot and look to impress with an extra bit of panache or a greater stunt. Attempt the triggering check again, using the second result. On a success, you gain the normal results of the check, plus you feel invigorated by your stunt and gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level (double your level on a critical success). You lose any remaining temporary Hit Points after 1 minute. Typically, a challenging task is one with at least a [standard DC for your level](/Rules.aspx?ID=554), though the difficulty may be higher depending on the situation. A meaningful context is one where the action's success or failure is relevant to the pursuit of your goals.

[Showstopper](/Feats.aspx?ID=3202) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 118

**Archetypes** [Bullet Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=117) (Level 16), [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=120) (Level 16), [Bullet Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=364) (Level 16), [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=367) (Level 16)

**Prerequisites**
[Pistol Twirl](/Feats.aspx?ID=3162); Master in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

Your twirling weapons create a grand distraction that's difficult to look away from. When using Pistol Twirl to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48), you can target all enemies within your weapon's first range increment who you can perceive and who can see you. You roll one [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check and compare it against each target's Perception DC.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Evolution" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=394" />
<trait label="Summoner" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=392" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 69

</column>

---

Your eidolon can shrink to fit into small spaces. Your eidolon reduces in size, to a minimum of size Small. It can use this action again while shrunk to return to its normal size. Its [reach](/Rules.aspx?ID=2379) becomes 5 feet, or 10 feet if shrinking to Large with [Towering Size](/Feats.aspx?ID=2932).

<title level="2">Shrink Down leads to...</title>
[Miniaturize](/Feats.aspx?ID=2921)

    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shrink Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9393) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

**Prerequisites**
[Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4994)

</column>

---

You’ve learned to manipulate space to narrow the impact of other spells. When you use [Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4994) to attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) a spell that has an area of a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), or [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) and does not have a duration, you reduce the area of the spell if you fail to counteract it. Remove 5 feet from the radius of a burst or [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) or 10 feet from the length of a cone or line.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shroud of Ghosts](/Feats.aspx?ID=7186) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 41

**Usage**
imbued into a worn ikon

</column>

---

Your ikon is connected to the world of the spirits, allowing you to partially fade into their realm. The imbued ikon gains the following ability. 

 **Transcendence—Skirt the Underworld** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (concentrate, illusion, incapacitation, transcendence) You skirt into the world of the dead, becoming [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) for 1 round, then Fly up to your Speed. Each enemy adjacent to you at any point during this movement must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or become [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 minute (or permanently on a critical failure). For each creature blinded by this effect, the duration of the granted invisibility extends by 1 round. Undead and other creatures with strong ties to the world of the dead, such as psychopomps, are immune to this effect.

You've learned to camouflage yourself among the shadows and currents of the ocean so you're hard to see from above. When you're fully underwater, you're [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to all opponents who are out of the water, and [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) to those who are out of the water and more than 10 feet away from you.

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 262

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14)

</column>

---

You learn the sign languages associated with the languages you know, allowing you to sign and understand signs. Sign languages typically require both hands to convey more complex concepts, and they are visual rather than auditory.

Sign language is difficult to understand during combat due to the level of attention needed, unlike basic gestures like pointing at a foe to suggest a target. Sign language is hard to use in areas of low visibility, just like speech is difficult in a noisy environment.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 233 **Prerequisites** [Magical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5178); Master in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) --- Magic items you create bear a stamp specific to your handiwork. When you successfully [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) a permanent magic item, roll a DC 9 flat check when the item is fully complete. Any benefit a creature gains from an item quirk applies only while the creature wears the item (for a worn item) or holds it (for a held item). The GM might allow custom quirks similar to those listed. **Critical Success** Choose an item quirk from the table and its specifics.
**Success** The item gains a random item quirk with any specifics selected by the GM.
d10 QuirkDescription
1 Cavorting Dances in place when not in use.
2 Clean Remains pristine despite filth
3 Environmental Appearance changes to match its environment.
4 Filthy A layer of filth always remains.
5 Floating Slowly descends when dropped.
6 Glittering Shimmers and glows with light bright as a torch.
7 Invisible The item is invisible, but becomes visible for 1 round after being used.
8 Loyal Floats within 5 feet of its owner, as if on a tether (but can still be seized by someone else).
9 Mood coloration
 User's mood affects the item's color.
10 Skillful The item grants a +1 item bonus to one type of skill checks.

fields.text: Feat 7 Signature Crafting Uncommon General Skill Source Player Core 2 pg. 233 Prerequisites Magical Crafting; Master in Crafting Magic items you create bear a stamp specific to your handiwork. When you successfully Craft a permanent magic item, roll a DC 9 flat check when the item is fully complete. Any benefit a creature gains from an item quirk applies only while the creature wears the item (for a worn item) or holds it (for a held item). The GM might allow custom quirks similar to those listed. Critical Success Choose an item quirk from the table and its specifics. Success The item gains a random item quirk with any specifics selected by the GM. d10 Quirk Description 1 Cavorting Dances in place when not in use. 2 Clean Remains pristine despite filth 3 Environmental Appearance changes to match its environment. 4 Filthy A layer of filth always remains. 5 Floating Slowly descends when dropped. 6 Glittering Shimmers and glows with light bright as a torch. 7 Invisible The item is invisible, but becomes visible for 1 round after being used. 8 Loyal Floats within 5 feet of its owner, as if on a tether (but can still be seized by someone else). 9 Mood coloration User's mood affects the item's color. 10 Skillful The item grants a +1 item bonus to one type of skill checks.

Your energy saturates one of your weapons; it might be one inherited or one tied to your history. Pick a weapon and give it a name; this weapon gains the [unique](/Traits.aspx?ID=723) trait. You gain access to its [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203) effect. You can spend one action saying the name of your weapon, summoning it into your empty hand if the weapon is unattended and within 1 mile; this is an [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effect.

If your signature weapon is destroyed, you can spend three days and three nights saturating a new weapon with your energy, creating a new signature weapon.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Avenger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=282)

**Prerequisites**
[Avenger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7232)

**Trigger**
A creature you can [observe](/Conditions.aspx?ID=84) within reach of your deity’s favored weapon casts a spell.

**Requirements**
You are wielding your deity’s [favored weapon](/Rules.aspx?ID=805)

</column>

---

Your training included instruction on how to prevent enemy priests from using their magic against you, a technique you have mastered and adapted. Make a Strike with your deity's favored weapon against the triggering creature. On a success, the target is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your next turn. The triggering spell is disrupted on a critical success, or on a success if the target is your hunted prey and the spell is a [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) spell.

**Special** If your deity’s favored weapon is a ranged weapon, this reaction can trigger if the target is within its first range increment and you can make a ranged Strike instead of a melee Strike.

**Prerequisites**
[Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=640)

</column>

---

You’ve learned how to cast many of your spells without speaking the words of power you would normally need to provide. If the next action you use is Casting a Spell that has a verbal component and at least one other component, you can remove the verbal component. This makes the spell quieter and allows you to cast it in areas where sound can’t carry. However, the spell still has visual manifestations, so this doesn’t make the spell any less obvious to someone who sees you casting it. When you use Silent Spell, you can choose to gain the benefits of Conceal Spell, and you don’t need to attempt a Deception check because the spell has no verbal components.

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**

**Trigger**

---

You quickly hide your weapon to make it difficult to pin the attack on you. You attempt to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) to hide the triggering weapon. Your Stealth check is compared to the Perception DC of all creatures within 30 feet that can see you. You automatically succeed against creatures farther than 30 feet. The target of your Strike gains a +4 circumstance bonus to their Perception DC for this check. If your Stealth check is a success, you hide your weapon so well that the creature can't clearly determine where the attack originated.

---

You've lived in the shadow of the Shattered Range, and the patience of those ancient mountains expresses itself in your stillness. Your body might have veins of granite, sandstone, or similar sedimentary rocks that make it easier for you to camouflage yourself in certain regions. You become trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15), and you gain the [Terrain Stalker](/Feats.aspx?ID=852) skill feat. If you're already trained in Stealth from another source, you become trained in a skill of your choice instead.

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 110 **Prerequisites** [armor innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=1), [construct innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=2), or [weapon innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=3) **Access** Tian Xia origin --- Taking inspiration from [Desna’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=281) image as a giant silk moth in Tian Xia, you’ve attached a bracelet to your innovation that generates ultra-strong silk strands mixed with venom. You can unleash this substance as part of an attack. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306). If it hits, the target takes damage from the Strike as normal and must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC with the following effects. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The silk imposes a –10 foot status penalty to all the target’s Speeds for 1 round.
**Failure** As success, and the target takes an additional 1d4 [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). The poison damage increases to 2d4 at 12th level and 3d4 at 18th level.
**Critical Failure** As failure, and the target is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until the end of their next turn.

>
[Sinbladed Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7486) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

**Prerequisites**

---

You punctuate your spellcasting with a flourish of your weapon, imparting physical force to your magic. If the next spell you cast is a non-cantrip sin or curriculum spell that affects a single target, and you either succeed on your attack roll or the target fails its saving throw against the spell, a wound in the shape of your personal rune appears on the target, dealing additional persistent bleed damage equal to the spell’s rank, in addition to its regular effects.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Sing to the Steel](/Feats.aspx?ID=3042) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Nantambu Chime-Ringer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=106)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Nantambu Chime-Ringer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3039)

</column>

---

You strike magical tones that can turn the tide of combat. You and your allies within 30 feet gain the effects of one of the following runes until the end of your next turn: [_corrosive_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=292), [_disrupting_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=294), [_flaming_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295), [_frost_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=296), [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297), [_shock_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=303), or [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=306). The effects apply to a single weapon the creature is holding or one of the creature's [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks. You choose the rune and the effect applies to all creatures. You can use an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, to extend the duration of the rune for 1 additional round up to a maximum of 1 minute. If this would give a weapon or unarmed attack more property runes than its normal maximum, an existing property rune (as the creature chooses) is suppressed until the spell ends.

You possess horns, a tail, or red eyes, or could otherwise be mistaken for a [tiefling](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=26). You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7). If you would automatically become trained in Intimidation (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the [Intimidating Glare](/Feats.aspx?ID=796) skill feat, as well as a +2 circumstance bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) when pretending to be a version of yourself who is a tiefling.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 57

**Prerequisites**
You've been brought to 0 Hit Points by an enemy that has the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait or an enemy's ability that has the water trait.

</column>

---

Your body looks like it's made of flowing water, clear and pristine, providing a natural grace to all your movements. You gain a swim Speed equal to your land Speed. If you already had a swim Speed, it's increased by 10 feet. You gain the Water Transfer activity, which enables you to teleport through a body of water.

 **Water Transfer** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Requirements** You're on land and adjacent to a body of water; **Effect** You sink into the water and emerge back onto land in another space within 120 feet that's adjacent to the same body of water. You can transport yourself, any items you're wearing and holding, and up to one other willing creature.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

Like how a constrictor wraps itself around its next meal, your companion tightens its teeth around its constrained prey to squeeze the life out of it. Your companions with a qualifying unarmed attack learn the Sinking Jaws activity.

fields.text: Feat 10 Siphon Life Two Actions Rare Aftermath Magical Void Source Dark Archive (Remastered) pg. 56 Prerequisites You've been reduced to 0 Hit Points by an enemy with the void trait. Experiences with necromantic energy have left a permanent mark on you, casting you in a deathlike pallor, chilling your body temperature to be ice-cold, turning your very blood black, and giving you the power to rip out an enemy's life force. Strike with an unarmed attack. If you hit and the target is a living creature, it takes 4d6 additional void damage, depending on its Fortitude save. <traits>

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 105

**Frequency**
once per day

**Requirements**
You haven't acted yet on your turn.

---

You draw upon the reservoir of your patron's magic that resides within your familiar. During your turn, you can cast one spell your familiar knows that was granted by your patron's theme or lessons without spending a spell slot to do so (or even having it prepared). The spell must be at least 1 level lower than your highest-level witch spell slot.

**Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of spells you cast ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)).

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 38 **Frequency** once per day **Prerequisites** Expert in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) --- You can beguile and bewitch with your song. All creatures in a 60-foot emanation must attempt a Will save against your Performance DC. On subsequent rounds, you can Sustain the song, causing each creature in the area currently affected by your song to attempt another Will save. Typically, creatures that have traveled with you for a significant time, such as your fellow party members, are immune to your Siren Song. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected and becomes immune to your Siren Song for 24 hours.
**Success** The target is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) with you until the end of your next turn.
**Failure** As success, and the target is [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for as long as it's fascinated.
**Critical Failure** As success, and the target is stupefied 2 for as long as it's fascinated.

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 109

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) This feat does not allow Pathfinder Society members to become unholy or add the unholy trait to their weapons._

**Archetype** [Sister of the Golden Erinys](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=380)

**Access**
You're from Isger or a member of the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys.

</column>

---

The fighting style of the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys is rooted in their understanding of devils. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for Devil Lore. When you choose this feat, you can choose to become sanctified as unholy. You gain access to the asp coil. You have familiarity with the [asp coil](/Weapons.aspx?ID=233) and [scourge](/Weapons.aspx?ID=531), treating them as simple weapons for the purposes of proficiency. If you're unholy, your Strikes using those weapons and your unarmed Strikes gain the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait.

**Special** If you have the [Monastic Weaponry](/Feats.aspx?ID=5979) feat, the asp coil gains the monk trait for you.

<title level="2">Sister of the Golden Erinys Dedication leads to...</title>
[Eye for Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=8931), [Fiendish Brand](/Feats.aspx?ID=8932), [Golden Erinys Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=8930), [Promise of Pain](/Feats.aspx?ID=8935), [Vengeance Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=8933), [Wrathful Presence](/Feats.aspx?ID=8936)

You stand firm, steeling your mind and body, allowing you to use your magic unperturbed. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sixth Sense](/Feats.aspx?ID=3670) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 26

</column>

---

Your psychic abilities also allow you to detect the lingering thoughts of spirits and similar entities. While you're exploring but not [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519), the GM rolls a secret check for you to find [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) that usually require Searching, as well as [spirits](/Traits.aspx?ID=149), creatures on the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=9), and beings made entirely of spiritual essence, such as [celestials](/Traits.aspx?ID=23), [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=70), and [monitors](/Traits.aspx?ID=111).

 You can also potentially notice [ethereal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=284) creatures and spirits inside solid objects, provided they are within 30 feet of you. This applies while Searching, [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=84), and on the automatic secret check from Sixth Sense. You can still notice spirits only on a successful check, and you can't see them if they're more than 5 feet inside an object.

 When you notice a creature with your Sixth Sense, you also learn its location, making it [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to you if it had been [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 38

---

You make use of what remains of a thrall to extend your limbs to unnatural lengths. If the next action you take is to cast a grave spell that destroys a thrall, pieces of the thrall fuse with you to extend the length of your limbs. Until the end of the turn, your reach increases by 10 feet, and you can move 15 feet whenever you [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Skeleton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=236" />

Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

You gain the ability to summon your own skeletal minions. You learn the [_create undead_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=10) rituals to create three types of undead for which you meet the prerequisites. These undead must have the [skeleton](/Traits.aspx?ID=236) trait or be other skeletal undead the GM agrees to. You can't teach these rituals to anyone else, and you can't participate in either ritual while allowing someone else to serve as the primary caster unless they also know the ritual.

 You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Religion checks for _create undead_ rituals. You can also perform the ritual without the aid of a secondary caster; in this case, you attempt the secondary check normally performed by that caster.

[Skeptic's Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=3777) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 79

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7)

**Trigger**
You are targeted by or are in the area of a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) spell or effect.

</column>

---

You don't believe in any mental twaddle, and you're certainly not afraid of it. You scoff and verbally refute the triggering effect, attempting a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check using your Intimidation modifier with a counteract level of half your level rounded up. If you succeed, you ignore the triggering effect, though any other creatures that were also targeted or in the area are still affected. If the source of the effect you successfully counteracted understands your language and has an Intelligence modifier of –3 or higher, that creature becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for 1 round.

You've been taught how to craft healing remedies with a variety of herbs and plants. You can use [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) an [alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528) item that has the [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) trait, rather than [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37).

You claw open the top layer of your scales and peel off the premature shed in order to remove harmful substances from your skin. You immediately end all [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) from effects that coat your skin (such as fire and most persistent acid damage). If you're suffering from an effect other than persistent damage that depends on continuous contact with your skin, and if that effect allows a saving throw, immediately attempt a new saving throw against that effect.

</column>

---

Your mask holds the legacy of Black Heron, the Wings of Knowledge, who united the aeromancers of the Shory Empire. You can harness residual magical power to fly. You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only you, your fly Speed doubles until your next turn.

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. For instance, the Cunning Trickster mask could easily be a rodent or a fox, not just a spider.

**Related Feats**: [Cunning Trickster Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3433), [Emancipator's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3434), [Grand Medic's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3435), [Protective Spirit Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3436), [Stalking Feline Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3438), [Storyteller's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3439), [Thick Hide Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3440), [Tireless Guide's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3441), [Vigilant Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3442)

<traits>

<trait label="Electricity" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=56" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Sonic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=147" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 225

**Archetype** [Jalmeri Heavenseeker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=198)

**Prerequisites**
[Sky and Heaven Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2200)

**Requirements**
You are in Sky and Heaven Stance.

</column>

---

You [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81) toward an opponent. At any point in the Leap, you can make a single Strike against a creature within your reach. At 12th level, if you hit with this Strike, instead of finishing your Leap, you can immediately attempt a second Leap from the space where you struck the target of your Strike. You can make a single Strike against a target within your reach during this second Leap as well. At 16th level, you can attempt a third Leap if your second Strike hits, and you can attack a target at any point during this third Leap. All Leaps made during this activity gain a +10-foot status bonus to the total height or distance of your leap, and no two Strikes can target the same creature.

**Archetypes** [Mauler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=68) (Level 4), [Thlipit Contestant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=224) (Level 6), [Mauler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=256) (Level 4), [Rivethun Invoker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=309) (Level 6)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

You make an attack to knock a foe off balance, then follow up immediately with a sweep to topple them. Make a melee Strike. If it hits and deals damage, you can attempt an Athletics check to Trip the creature you hit. If you’re wielding a two-handed melee weapon, you can ignore Trip’s requirement that you have a hand free. Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both of them.

<title level="2">Slam Down leads to...</title>
[Crashing Slam](/Feats.aspx?ID=4821)

At 14th level, add adamantine and mithral to the list of materials you can choose from.

You've dedicated yourself to studying ancient techniques and memorized minor prayers against [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) to swiftly dispatch them. Make a Strike against a creature you know is undead. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, you deal one extra die of positive damage, with the same die size as the weapon or [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack you used. >
[Sleek Reposition](/Feats.aspx?ID=4786) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=601" />
<trait label="Press" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=133" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 143

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) If you're wielding a polearm, you can ignore Reposition's requirement that you have a hand free_

**Requirements**
You are wielding a finesse weapon or polearm

</column>

---

While your opponent is still recovering from your prior attack, you snag its armor, clothing, or flesh to move it as you please. Make a melee Strike with a finesse weapon or polearm. If you hit a target that is your size or smaller, you can automatically Reposition it, with the same benefits as the Reposition action (including the critical success effect, if your Strike was a critical hit). If you used a weapon with reach, use the weapon’s reach for this Reposition.

This Strike has the following failure effect.

**Failure** The target becomes [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your current turn.

---

Philosophers compare the cycle of life, death, and rebirth to sleeping, dreaming, and waking. You take it to another level by reliving previous lives in dreams, always waking invigorated and thankful for a new chance at life. Whenever you rest for 8 hours, you gain the effects of a long-term rest. If you're an ancestry that neither sleeps nor dreams, you still receive this benefit by entering a reflective, meditative state during rest.

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 206 **Archetype** [Sleepwalker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=195) **Prerequisites** Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) --- You've learned to manipulate states of consciousness, beginning with your own. You can send yourself into a half-awake, daydreaming state and gain the Daydream Trance action. **Daydream Trance** ([enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) You fall into a half-sleeping trance. This lasts for 1 minute or until you fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), whichever comes first. You can voluntarily end your trance by taking a single action, which has a [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, and succeeding at a Will save against your own class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Once your trance ends, you can't enter a Daydream Trance again for 1 minute. While you're in your trance, you gain the following effects:
  • You gain a +1 status bonus to Will saves. This bonus increases to +2 against mental effects. If you're legendary in Occultism, the bonus against mental effects increases to +3.
  • You take a –1 penalty to Perception checks and initiative rolls.
**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the sleepwalker archetype. Sleepwalker Dedication leads to... [Dream Logic](/Feats.aspx?ID=3880), [Dream Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=3876), [Ever Dreaming](/Feats.aspx?ID=3882), [Infiltrate Dream](/Feats.aspx?ID=3874), [Shared Dream](/Feats.aspx?ID=3881), [Vision of Foresight](/Feats.aspx?ID=3875), [Waking Dream](/Feats.aspx?ID=3877), [Ward Slumber](/Feats.aspx?ID=3879)

<title level="2">Gang Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing](/Sources.aspx?ID=48) pg. 75

Street gangs in Absalom recruit amateur pickpockets, ruffians, and vandals who show promise in their specialties and operate well in tight groups.

 Rogue agents can gain access to some of the following rogue feats by successfully helping Maurrisa Jonne or Bloody Berleth eliminate their rival (see Chapter 1). Some of these feats, however, can be gained only by helping a particular side in the gang conflict.

**Related Feats**: [Ambushing Knockdown](/Feats.aspx?ID=2207), [Coordinated Distraction](/Feats.aspx?ID=2210), [Deny Support](/Feats.aspx?ID=2209), [Subtle Shank](/Feats.aspx?ID=2208)

You can move through gloom with the speed of darkness. You can move 5 feet farther when you take the [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) action, up to your Speed. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Dhampir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=215" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 27

**Prerequisites**
ability to cast at least one spell with the [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) trait

</column>

---

Your shadow magic bleeds into the space around you. Whenever you cast a spell with the darkness trait, a lingering aura of shadows reduces bright light within a 5-foot emanation around you to dim light until the end of your turn. Like in natural dim light, you can use these shadows to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62), but the aura still makes your overall position obvious, so you can't become [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) through the use of these shadows alone.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 75

**Prerequisites**
[Thlipit Contestant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5474); unarmed attack with your tongue

</column>

---

Your tongue darts out in search of refreshment. Choose a liquid container of up to light Bulk within reach of your lash, such as a [potion](/Traits.aspx?ID=672) or [elixir](/Traits.aspx?ID=589). The container must be held or in the open, not stowed in a pack or bandoleer. If the container is unattended or held by a willing ally, you Interact to drink the contents. If the container is held by an unwilling creature, you must succeed on a check using your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack modifier or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) modifier against the creature's Reflex DC to drink the contents; this adds the [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540) trait.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 174

**Prerequisites**
[sneak attack](/Classes.aspx?ID=10)

</column>

---

Your attacks deal more damage, even against creatures that aren’t off-guard. When you succeed or critically succeed at a Strike against a creature that isn’t off-guard, you also deal 1d6 precision damage. This applies only if you’re using a weapon or unarmed attack you could deal sneak attack damage with.

At 14th level, if you would normally deal 3d6 or more sneak attack damage to off-guard creatures, you deal 2d6 precision damage to creatures that aren’t off-guard.

You single out one enemy to destroy in your deity's name. Designate one enemy you can see. Until the start of your next turn, your Strikes against that enemy gain a +3 status bonus to damage, increasing to +4 if you have master proficiency with the weapon or unarmed attack you're using for the Strike. If you're [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) and the target has the opposite trait, the bonus is +4 (or +6 if you're a master).

 If the target takes a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against you or one of your allies before the start of your next turn, the duration extends to the end of that enemy's next turn. If the enemy continues to take these hostile actions each turn, the duration continues to extend.

 Your current Smite ends if you use the Smite action again.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

You can add a tarry additive to an alchemical bomb to make it emit smoke. When thrown, in addition to its normal effects, the bomb creates a cloud of smoke in a 10-foot burst. You choose which corner of the target's space (or the space in which the bomb lands) the cloud is centered on. Creatures within that area have the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition, and all other creatures are concealed to them. The smoke lasts for 1 minute or until dissipated by a strong wind.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 115

**Requirements**
You're wielding a loaded firearm and are wearing or holding a dose of black powder.

</column>

---

You load an extra dose of powder into your shot, causing it to belch a cloud of smoke. You make a Strike with your firearm and create a cloud of smoke in a 20-foot emanation centered on your location. Creatures are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) while within the smoke, and creatures outside the area are concealed to creatures within the smoke. The smoke dissipates at the start of your next turn. If your Strike is a critical failure, your firearm [misfires](/Rules.aspx?ID=1649).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Jotunborn" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=860" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 15

</column>

---

You stomp and unleash a wave of the magic of creation in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) that transforms non-magical [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and greater difficult terrain into normal terrain. This terrain transformation remains in place for 1 minute, after which the terrain returns to its original state.

Your stomp can also [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) magical difficult terrain and magical greater difficult terrain. Your stomp’s counteract rank equals half your level (rounded up), and for the roll, use either your class DC – 10 or your spellcasting attribute modifier plus your spellcasting proficiency bonus. If you successfully counteract the triggering effect, you suppress the effect for 1 minute, after which the effect returns if its duration hasn’t expired.

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 41 **Archetype** [Pathfinder Agent](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=13) **Prerequisites** Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9); [Pathfinder Agent Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=871) --- Pathfinders are trained to help each other be safe and successful, and you know how to jolt your allies back to their senses. You’ve learned to react with ranged weapons when a creature is in close quarters. You can use a reaction that normally allows you to make a melee weapon Strike to instead make a ranged weapon Strike. You must be Striking an adjacent target. If necessary for the reaction’s trigger, you treat your ranged weapon as if it had a reach of 5 feet. If the reaction has other requirements, such as wielding a specific kind of weapon, Snap Shot doesn’t allow you to ignore them; it allows you only to replace a melee weapon Strike with a ranged weapon Strike.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Kobold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=224" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 15

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The snares created with this feat are temporary items and become unusable after 24 hours or during your next daily preparations, whichever comes first._

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4); [Snare Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=843)

</column>

---

Your expertise makes your snares more powerful, and you can place them quickly and efficiently. Each day during your daily preparations, you can prepare three [snares](/Equipment.aspx?Category=31) from your formula book for quick deployment; if the snare normally takes 1 minute to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43), you can Craft it with 3 Interact actions. Snares prepared in this way don't cost you any resources to Craft. The number of snares you can prepare this way increases to four if you are a master in Crafting, and to five if you are legendary.

 When you Craft and deploy a snare that deals damage, any creature that critically fails its saving throw against the snare's initial effect and takes damage becomes [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the end of its next turn.

[Sniping Duo Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3258) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 137

**Archetype** [Sniping Duo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=121)

**Prerequisites**
trained in at least one type of weapon in the [crossbow](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=17) or [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16) groups; Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

When you take this dedication, choose one willing, non-[minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) ally to act as your spotter. As part of your training in this archetype, you train your spotter in the necessary habits and techniques to use your abilities automatically; your spotter doesn't need to spend any feats of their own to grant the effects. You only gain the benefits of your Sniping Duo archetype feats if both you and your spotter are alive and conscious. You and your spotter don't grant your foes lesser cover against one another's Strikes. Whenever you or your spotter successfully Strikes a target, the other member of your duo gains a +1 circumstance bonus per weapon damage die on the damage roll of their next Strike made against that target before the end of their next turn.

 You can change your designated spotter by spending 3 days of downtime training with another ally.

<title level="2">Sniping Duo Dedication leads to...</title>
[Concentrated Assault](/Feats.aspx?ID=3266), [Duo's Aim](/Feats.aspx?ID=3262), [Eagle Eyes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3265), [Exploit Opening](/Feats.aspx?ID=3260), [Tag Team](/Feats.aspx?ID=3264), [Targeted Redirection](/Feats.aspx?ID=3261), [Triangulate](/Feats.aspx?ID=3259), [Vantage Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3263)

You and your spotter don’t grant your foes lesser [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) against one another’s Strikes. Whenever you or your spotter successfully Strikes a target, the other member of your duo gains a +1 circumstance bonus per weapon damage die on the damage roll of their next Strike made against that target before the end of their next turn.

You can change your designated spotter by spending 3 days of downtime training with another ally.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you’ve gained two other feats from the sniping duo archetype.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Lineage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=317" />

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 22

---

You're the child of a winter hag, with one blue-white eye and an affinity for rime and snow. When moving over ice or snow in arctic terrain, you always gain the benefits of the [Cover Tracks](/Actions.aspx?ID=65) action without needing to use the activity or having to move half your Speed. You don't treat icy terrain as uneven ground (though it's still difficult terrain for you), and you ignore difficult terrain caused by snow. Cold precipitation and environmental cold effects don't alter the time it takes for you to become fatigued.

<title level="2">Snow May leads to...</title>
[Invoke the Elements](/Feats.aspx?ID=2337)

The howling wind and precipitation of your magic turn to thick snow. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that has the air, water, or cold trait, and that does not have the fire trait, select one creature affected by the spell on the ground. Each square on the ground under or adjacent to the creature fills with ankle-deep snow. Those squares are difficult terrain until the beginning of your next turn. A creature can Interact to clear a square of snow, and the snow in a square melts if that square is exposed to a fire effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Vishkanya" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=369" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 61

</column>

---

You have the uncanny ability to quickly blend into the lifestyle of whatever settlement in which you find yourself. After residing in a particular settlement for at least 1 day, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) to pass yourself off as a resident of that settlement. Additionally, you can use [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) in place of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) while in that settlement. The GM might decide you need more time in particularly large settlements to gain these benefits, or might decide you gain the benefits only while in a specific district or part of the settlement.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 196

**Archetype** [Vigilante](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=80)

**Prerequisites**
[Vigilante Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2083)

</column>

---

You have built a reputation for yourself in your social identity. Choose one archetype that you meet the prerequisites for. You gain that archetype's dedication feat and can select feats from that archetype, even if you haven't yet gained enough feats in the vigilante archetype to take another dedication feat. These feats become part of your social identity and gain the social trait—for instance, a [fighter](/Classes.aspx?ID=7) vigilante could take the [wizard dedication](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=12) feat and have a [wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=12) social identity. Using these feats in your social identity doesn't risk exposing your vigilante identity, but using them in your vigilante identity could put you at risk for exposure.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 61

</column>

---

Sometimes your case splinters into smaller mysteries, but you never lose sight of the big picture. Once per day when you give up on the subject of a lead due to using [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=544) again, you can designate the lead you stopped pursuing as your solid lead for the day. Even though you stopped following the solid lead, you can change back to your solid lead any number of times by using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. Doing so ends one of your current leads as normal.

 During your next daily preparations, you can maintain your solid lead or you can remove it; removing it allows you to designate a new solid lead later that day.

    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Solidarity](/Feats.aspx?ID=6877) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Poppet" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=418" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 49

**Frequency**
Once per 10 Minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Tsukumogami Poppet](/Heritages.aspx?ID=383) heritage

</column>

---

You bestow some of your own life energies to mend damage. You touch a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less, and you restore Hit Points to the target equal to twice your level. You lose as many Hit Points as the target regained. This direct transfer of vitality means that no effects apply that would increase the Hit Points the target regains or decrease the Hit Points you lose. This transfer also ignores any temporary Hit Points you or the target have. You can’t reduce your Hit Points below 1 using Solidarity. You can’t replace lost pieces or repair an object that has been completely destroyed.

**Special** If you have the [Minuscule Mentee](/Feats.aspx?ID=6580) feat, you can use Solidarity to heal your familiar.

</column>

---

Choose an additional soulforged armament of a different type than the type you already chose, and choose one essence power for it. Upgrade and change armaments individually.

 When you [Manifest Soulforged Armament](/Feats.aspx?ID=3016), you can summon any number of your armaments (you must meet the Requirements for each), and when you Dismiss the effect, you can choose to Dismiss some and not others. You can choose to manifest the essence form of any number of your armaments when you take the action. Each armament can manifest its essence form only once per day.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 236

**Archetype** [Soulforger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=102)

**Prerequisites**
[Soulforger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3016)

**Trigger**
An attack you made with a soulforged weapon or shield misses a creature, or a creature hits you with an attack while you're either wearing manifested soulforged armor or have your soulforged shield raised.

**Requirements**
Your soulforged armament is manifested.

</column>

---

You strive to change the outcome with sheer zeal. You gain a +1 status bonus to your attack roll if making an attack or to your AC if you were hit. This can change the outcome of the roll. If this bonus turns your missed attack into a hit or the hit against you into a miss, attempt a DC 5 flat check. If you fail, your soulforged armament is Dismissed—your weapon if you attacked or your armor or shield if you were defending.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 125

**Archetype** [Splinter of Finality](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=317)

**Prerequisites**
[Spectral Dagger](/Feats.aspx?ID=7704)

**Trigger**
You reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with an attack from your _spectral dagger_.

**Requirements**
Your [_splinter of finality's_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772)  doesn’t contain a trapped soul.

</column>

---

Your mortal strike wrenches the soul from your victim’s body and imprisons it in your [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772), with the effects of [_seize soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1664). The _splinter of finality_ can only hold one soul at a time, but you can release a trapped soul as a free action. If you don’t free a soul willingly, it escapes automatically after 24 hours. However, if you touch the _splinter of finality_ to an unbroken final blade while a soul is trapped within, the soul is transferred to the [_final blade_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094) and imprisoned indefinitely. 

While your _splinter of finality_ contains a trapped soul, you gain [fast healing](/Rules.aspx?ID=2322) 15.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Soul Thief](/Feats.aspx?ID=9167) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 41

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
You are [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521).

</column>

---

You attempt to steal the soul of a creature that was at least 18th level that died within the last minute. Attempt an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check against the hard DC of the [target’s level](/Rules.aspx?ID=2629). On a success, you capture its soul and solidify it into a gem that keeps the soul contained. While the soul is contained, it can’t be returned to life through any means, even powerful magic such as the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual. If a gem is destroyed, the soul is freed, and you become alerted to its destruction. You can maintain only three gems at any given time. If you attempt to make a fourth, you must choose a soul to be released. 

You can consume a captured soul by swallowing a gem. Doing so grants you the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) traits and extends your existence by 50 years. You gain [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83), you aren’t instantly destroyed when reduced to 0 Hit Points, and you can’t be instantly killed by [death effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331). If you’re destroyed, you can rebuild yourself in the location of one of your soul gems. This consumes the gem, and it takes 24 hours for your body to be rebuilt. If you are ever destroyed and are unable to rebuild your body, all souls that you have consumed are released.

    right="Feat 18"

>
[Soul Vessel Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=7318) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 109

**Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287)

**Prerequisites**
[Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304)

</column>

---

Your mount has a supernatural hunger for mortal souls that you can feed. Once per day, you can cast [_seize soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1664) as a divine innate spell. The spell gains a cost of 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) but you can use your apocalypse mount as the item in which you store the soul. Your apocalypse mount counts as an [artifact](/Traits.aspx?ID=537) for the purpose of the spell. At any point while your apocalypse mount contains a soul, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) the spell to allow your apocalypse mount to consume the soul. It regains a number of Hit Points equal to twice your level. For the next minute, it also gains a +20-foot status bonus to its Speed and its unarmed attack [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) are made at mythic proficiency.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Soul Warden Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3466) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 26

**Archetype** [Soul Warden](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=173)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); worships [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) or a psychopomp usher

</column>

---

You can take 10 minutes to emblazon Pharasma's holy sigil—a spiraling comet that represents the winding path a soul takes through its existence—upon a shield, tabard, banner, or other prominent object that your wear or wield. The symbol doesn't fade until 1 year has passed, but if you emblazon the symbol again, any symbol you previously emblazoned and any symbol already emblazoned on that item instantly disappears. The item becomes a [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) of Pharasma and can be used as a divine focus while emblazoned.

 Whenever an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature or captive soul is within 100 feet of this object, the spiral glows, shedding dim blue light in a 10-foot radius. If the creature is hiding or the soul is hidden, it must succeed at a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against your Perception DC to fool the sigil and prevent the spiral from glowing.

 In addition, you can cast [_disrupt undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=79) as a divine innate cantrip at will. As normal, a cantrip is automatically heightened to half your level rounded up. You gain access to the Cast a Spell activity if you didn't have it already. You're trained in divine spell attack rolls and spell DCs. Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Wisdom.

 When you have at least two other feats from this archetype, the spiral glows with [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 10-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 10 feet). Feats that require a creature or object to be in the light of your spiral function whether it's in the bright or dim light.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the soul warden archetype.

Your brush your fingers across your [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772), momentarily creating a metaphysical vortex from which mortal spirits struggle to escape. For the next minute, [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) treat all squares within 30 feet of you as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and living creatures within the same area die from the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition at dying 5 rather than dying 4. As it comes close to tasting a living soul, the _splinter of finality_ is empowered. If a living creature’s dying value increases while within your Soul Well, your _spectral dagger_ deals one additional weapon die of damage until the end of your next turn.

>
[Soulforger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3016) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 236

**Archetype** [Soulforger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=102)

**Prerequisites**
Wisdom 14 or ability to cast [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells

</column>

---

You can manifest the power of your spirit in combat to realize your motivations. You manifest an armor, shield, or weapon as a [soulforged armament](/Rules.aspx?ID=1561). Choose one essence power for the armament (below). Changing an essence power requires 1 week of retraining, and you can't retrain it while you have soulforged corruption.

 You can Manifest Soulforged Armament to summon your armaments in combat.

 **Manifest Soulforged Armament** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67)) **Requirements** If summoning a weapon or shield, you have the hands free to wield it; if summoning armor, you aren't wearing any armor; **Effect** You immediately wield or wear the soulforged armament bound to you. The soulforged armament remains manifested until you Dismiss this effect.

 Once per day when you use this ability, you can manifest the armament's essence form. You gain the armament's essence power until it's Dismissed. After 1 minute, the essence form armament is automatically Dismissed.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat before gaining two other feats from this archetype.

<title level="2">Soulforger Dedication leads to...</title>
[Rapid Manifestation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3018), [Soul Arsenal](/Feats.aspx?ID=3019), [Soul Flare](/Feats.aspx?ID=3017)

The soulforged armament remains manifested until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this effect.

>
[Soulsight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1647) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=19" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 113

**Prerequisites**
[[Sorcerer](/Classes.aspx?ID=11)] bloodline that grants [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) or [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) spells

</column>

---

Your muse has opened your senses to the world beyond. You gain spiritsense as an imprecise sense with a range of 60 feet. Spiritsense enables you to sense the spirits of creatures, including living creatures, most non-mindless [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), and [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) within the listed range. As with your hearing and other imprecise senses, you still need to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) to locate an undetected creature. As spiritsense detects spiritual essence, not physical bodies, it can detect spirits projected by spells such as [_project image_](/Spells.aspx?ID=237) or possessing otherwise soulless objects. It can't detect soulless bodies, [constructs](/Traits.aspx?ID=35), or objects, and like most senses, it doesn't penetrate through solid objects.

<title level="2">Soulsight leads to...</title>
[Shared Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=3642)

</title>

<traits>

You twist not just the visual, but the auditory as well, allowing you to pass without a sound and create minor noises as distractions—perfect for misdirection and infiltration. You can cast [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=287) on yourself as a 2nd-level innate occult spell and [_ventriloquism_](/Spells.aspx?ID=356) as a 1st-level innate occult spell, both once per day. You also can cast [_ghost sound_](/Spells.aspx?ID=132) as an innate occult cantrip. You become trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs, and your key spellcasting ability is Charisma.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 71 **Prerequisites** Expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) **Access** members of the Firebrands gain access to them once they reach the rank of second mark --- You spread rumors, which may or may not be true, about a specific subject. If the subject of your rumor is not currently the subject of any contradictory rumors, this takes as long as it would normally take you to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) (typically 2 hours), at the end of which the GM rolls a secret Deception check to see how well you spread the rumor. If your rumor matches any current rumors about the subject, it takes less time to spread the rumor, and if you are attempting to overtake a particularly popular and contradictory rumor, it takes much longer or may be impossible. The DC similarly increases or decreases depending on how plausible your rumor is. **Critical Success** Your rumor spreads like wildfire. Anyone who succeeds at a check to Gather Information on the specific subject learns your rumor in preference to other rumors about the subject. Your rumor persists for 1 month.
**Success** You successfully spread the rumor. Anyone who succeeds at a check to Gather Information on the specific subject adds your rumor to the list of rumors they could learn about the subject. Your rumor persists for 1 week.
**Failure** Your rumor dies off, never becoming popular enough for other people to learn it via Gather Information.
**Critical Failure** You are unable to spread a rumor and take a –4 circumstance penalty to Deception checks to Sow Rumors about the same subject within the same region for 1 week. In addition, a rumor spreads about someone trying to spread false rumors about the subject. Firebrand Options **Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 71 The Firebrands use a variety of unorthodox equipment and techniques to achieve their goals, whether those goals include drawing attention, or subterfuge and subtlety. The following Firebrand options are uncommon, and members of the Firebrands gain access to them once they reach the rank of second mark. The [Entourage](/Feats.aspx?ID=1066) feat is rare even for members of the Firebrands, as it requires a certain degree of fame and in-world activity to acquire, and potentially requires the player or GM to keep track of additional background NPCs. Typically, only third mark and fourth mark Firebrands have the notoriety and social influence required to maintain an entourage. While Firebrands seek to build an entourage more than most adventurers, it’s not unreasonable for any famous character to gain access to it if the players are interested in playing with the [Entourage](/Feats.aspx?ID=1066) feat. **Related Feats**: [Backup Disguise](/Feats.aspx?ID=1064), [Entourage](/Feats.aspx?ID=1066)

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 234 **Prerequisites** Expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) --- You spread rumors, which may or may not be true, about a specific subject. If the subject of your rumor is not currently the subject of any contradictory rumors, this takes as long as it would normally take you to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) (typically 2 hours), at the end of which the GM rolls a secret Deception check against a DC they set to see how well you spread the rumor. If your rumor matches any current rumors about the subject, it takes less time to spread, and if you are attempting to overtake a particularly popular and contradictory rumor, it takes much longer or may be impossible. The DC similarly increases or decreases depending on how plausible your rumor is. For example, it might be harder to sow a rumor that the beloved, generous mayor is the head of a cult of murderous demon worshippers. **Critical Success** Your rumor spreads like wildfire. Anyone who succeeds at a check to Gather Information on the specific subject learns your rumor in preference to other rumors about the subject. Your rumor persists for 1 month. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Deception, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks in an appropriate situation when you invoke your rumor.
**Success** You successfully spread the rumor. Anyone who succeeds at a check to Gather Information on the specific subject adds your rumor to the list of rumors they could learn about the subject. Your rumor persists for 1 week. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, and Intimidation checks in an appropriate situation when you invoke your rumor.
**Failure** Your rumor dies off, never becoming popular enough for other people to learn it via Gather Information.
**Critical Failure** You are unable to spread a rumor and take a –4 circumstance penalty to Deception checks to Sow Rumors about the same subject within the same region for 1 week. In addition, a rumor spreads about someone trying to spread false rumors about the subject.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sow Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1719) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=52" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 125

</column>

---

You fold your spell into a seed. If your next action is to Cast a Spell using 1 action or 2 actions, the spell instead plants itself in an adjacent square. You must make all decisions regarding the spell at the time you cast it. Within the next 10 minutes, you can direct your sown spell to sprout and produce the spell's effects as a reaction, which is triggered when a creature enters the sown spell's space or a square adjacent to it. You can have only one sown spell at a time, and if you don't trigger the spell within 10 minutes, it dissipates and the spell is lost. A creature can notice the sown spell with a successful Perception check against your spell DC.

    right="Feat 12"

>
[Space-Time Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=3856) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 187

**Archetype** [Chronoskimmer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=192)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Chronoskimmer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3847)

**Trigger**
Your turn begins.

</column>

---

You travel just a few moments into the future to immediately arrive at your destination. Your Strides are augmented until the end of your turn, allowing you to instantly teleport to any point you could reach with your Stride instead of traversing normally to the location. Your augmented Strides have the [_teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=338) trait and don't trigger reactions that can be triggered by move actions or upon leaving or entering a square. You also augment your [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) actions in this way if you have the corresponding movement type.

You dust explosive black powder on your fist or glove before attacking, which combusts as you hit an opponent. The resulting pops of flame harm both you and your enemy. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />

You have become a divine entity, no longer entirely mortal. You no longer age, and you die only when you reach [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) 5 (dying 6 if you have [Diehard](/Feats.aspx?ID=5140)). Upon your death, your body and soul are transported to bask in the presence of your deity. Your god can decide to rebuild your mortal form and return you to the point of your death or some other safe location, or allow you to rest as an honored guest in their realm until you are needed once more. Typically, your god restores you if whatever quest you’re undertaking, such as defeating a malevolent tyrant or returning a stolen artifact, remains incomplete.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

---

Your study of different planes of existence makes you more attuned to teleportation effects. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus when you attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) a [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effect. 

When a teleportation effect occurs within 60 feet of you, you detect the location of the effect as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406). If the effect is a creature teleporting away from that space, you know the general direction of the location to which it teleported but not the distance. However, you can attempt to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) within an hour of the teleportation to know the location to which the creature teleported within 10 miles on a success or 1 mile on a critical success.

---

You channel the essences and echoes of spirits long dead that reside within a location, an object, or a bloodline. You spend 10 minutes and must be within the location, be able to touch a piece of the object, or drink a drop of blood of the bloodline as appropriate to the spirits you wish to channel. You learn one piece of information or about one significant event relating directly to the location, object, or bloodline that has occurred within the last year. You can channel any given target only once every 24 hours.

At 12th level, you can learn about information or events that took place within the last decade, within the last century if you are 16th level, or at any point in history at 20th level.

---

You've begun your training as a Speaker. Select divine or primal. If you selected divine, you're a Faithspeaker. If you selected primal, you're a Greenspeaker. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spear of Doom](/Feats.aspx?ID=7264) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 67

**Archetype** [Warrior Of Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=286)

**Prerequisites**
[Warrior Of Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7261)

**Requirements**
An enemy hit you with an attack dealing the same damage type as your cursed weakness within the last round, and you are [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1 or greater.

</column>

---

The conditions for your doom have been met, and you brace yourself for a battle that will see you either live to fight another day or die a legend. You enter the spear of doom stance. While in this stance, as long as the enemy who triggered your cursed weakness is within your reach, you can Strike them as a reaction whenever they succeed or critically succeed at an attack against you. You gain an additional reaction immediately and at the start of each of your subsequent turns that can only be used to make [Reactive Strikes](/Feats.aspx?ID=5832) against that opponent, or to make the [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) granted by this stance.

While in spear of doom stance, your cursed weakness is equal to your level instead of half your level.

<title level="2">Spear of Doom leads to...</title>
[Razor's Edge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7267)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Starlit Sentinel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=275)

**Prerequisites**
[Starlit Sentinel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7033)

</column>

---

You can channel the power of your constellation into a unique technique. You gain either the [_luminous stardust healing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2132) or [_shining starlight attack_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2133) [focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) spell, which you can cast only in sentinel form. When you gain this feat, decide a name for your technique, which becomes the spell's incantation. 

If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can Refocus by spending 10 minutes outside of your sentinel form to reflect on the values of your constellation. Starlit sentinel focus spells are [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) spells. You become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC, and your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

**Special** You can take this feat a second time, gaining the focus spell that you didn’t gain the first time.
