**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 262 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) --- Your training focused on Crafting one particular kind of item. Select one of the specialties listed below; you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to Craft items of that type. If you are a master in Crafting, this bonus increases to +2. If it’s unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides. Some specialties might apply only partially. For example, if you were making a morningstar and had specialty in woodworking, the GM might give you half your bonus because the item requires both blacksmithing and woodworking. ## Specialty Crafting
**Specialty****Applicable Items**
Alchemy*Alchemical items such as elixirs
ArtistryFine art, including jewelry
BlacksmithingDurable metal goods, including metal armor
BookmakingBooks and paper
GlassmakingGlass, including glassware and windows
LeatherworkingLeather goods, including leather armor
PotteryCeramic goods
ShipbuildingShips and boats
StonemasonryStone goods and structures
TailoringClothing
WeavingTextiles, baskets, and rugs
WoodworkingWooden goods and structures

* Requires [Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5117) to Craft. Specialty Crafting leads to... [Impeccable Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5158)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spectral Dagger](/Feats.aspx?ID=7704) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 124

**Archetype** [Splinter of Finality](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=317)

**Requirements**
You have a hand free and aren’t already wielding a _spectral dagger_.

</column>

---

By touching the [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772) in your neck, you conjure a _spectral dagger_ into your hand that resembles the splinter wrapped in a crude hilt. This weapon acts like a [_+1_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) [_dagger_](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358), and each successful [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with it deals 1 additional [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. If the attack is a critical hit, this damage increases to 1d6. If the _spectral dagger_ ever leaves your hand, it vanishes and you must spend an action to conjure it again. If this occurs as the result of you making a ranged thrown Strike with the dagger, you resolve the attack before the weapon vanishes.

You can increase the power of your _spectral dagger_ with runes like you can other weapons, transferring the rune from a runestone or other weapon by meditating over the rune as a downtime activity that takes 1 day.

<title level="2">Spectral Dagger leads to...</title>
[Dread Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7705), [Guillotine Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7712), [Hungry Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7709), [Lethal Edge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7708), [Soul Bleed](/Feats.aspx?ID=7706), [Soul Oubliette](/Feats.aspx?ID=7713)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spell Combination](/Feats.aspx?ID=5054) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=735" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 205

</column>

---

You can merge spells, producing multiple effects with a single casting. One slot of each rank of spell you can cast, except 2nd rank and 1st rank, becomes a spell combination slot (this doesn’t apply to cantrips). When you prepare your spells, you can fill a combination slot with a combination of two spells. Each spell in the combination must be 2 or more spell ranks below the slot’s rank, and both must target only one creature or object or have the option to target only one creature or object. Each spell in the combination must also have the same means of determining whether it has an effect—both spells must require a ranged spell attack, require the same type of saving throw, or automatically affect the target.

 When you cast a combined spell, it affects only one target, even if the component spells normally affect more than one. If any spell in the combination has further restrictions (such as targeting only living creatures), you must abide by all restrictions. The combined spell uses the shorter of the component spells’ ranges. Resolve a combined spell as if were a single spell, but apply the effects of both component spells. For example, if the spell’s target succeeded at the save against a combined spell, it would apply the success effect of each spell, and if it critically failed, it would apply the critical failure effect of both spells.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spell Crash](/Feats.aspx?ID=9064) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Force" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=75" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 21

**Prerequisites**
Your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) is charged, and you have at least one spell prepared in a spell slot.

</column>

---

Instead of blending a spell into an attack, you can funnel the spell’s magic into a pure blast that expands out from you. You smash your weapon or fist into the ground and expend a spell prepared in one of your spell slots. The magic of the spell explodes out in your choice of a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), 30-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), or 60-foot [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388). Each creature in the area takes 1d10 force damage per spell rank of the expended spell, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your spell DC. If your weapon has the [shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=694) trait, you push any creature that fails its save 10 feet; if your weapon has the [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=716) trait, any creature that fails its save falls prone. Your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) is no longer charged.

If the spell you expended could deal a type of damage other than force, you can change the explosion’s damage to that type and replace Spell Crash’s force trait with the corresponding trait.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 19

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The temporary Hit Points granted by the Spell Devourer orc ancestry feat are applied as soon as the character succeeds at their saving throw; for an effect that causes Hit Point damage on a successful save, such as a fireball, this means that the character gains the temporary Hit Points before taking damage._

**Prerequisites**
[Pervasive Superstition](/Feats.aspx?ID=89)

</column>

---

You don't just resist magic; you devour it. Whenever you succeed at a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you gain temporary Hit Points equal to double the spell's level, or equal to the level if the magical effect isn't a spell. These temporary Hit Points last until the end of your next turn.

**Prerequisites**
[Lich Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3513); Legendary in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

Inspired by the degenerate [demiliches](/Monsters.aspx?ID=283) your kind sometimes devolves into, you've embedded a gem into your brow, fusing it to your necrotic flesh. This gem has been specially calibrated to hold one of the following spells: [_repulsion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=254), [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268), or [_true seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344). You must decide which spell your gem contains when you take this feat; changing the spell requires retraining the feat. Once per day, you can drain the gem's magical energy to Cast the Spell without spending a spell slot.

 At 18th level, you can heighten whichever spell you chose to 7th level. At 20th level, you can heighten whichever spell you chose to 8th level; regardless of which spell you chose, you can instead drain the gem's magical energy to cast an 8th-level [_spell turning_](/Spells.aspx?ID=297) without spending a spell slot.

**Archetype** [Wildspell](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=295)

**Prerequisites**
[Wildspell Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7418)

**Trigger**
You cast [_spellsurge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2150).

</column>

---

Your aura links your friends together with mystic strands. While you’re in this stance, an ally within your spellsurge aura can treat any other ally within the aura as the point of origin for a spell they cast, calculating range and cover from the other creature’s space instead of their own. This allows all allied creatures within your spellsurge aura to act as though they’re in touch range of each other since each creature is in touch range of itself. Additionally, while you’re in this stance, an ally casting a spell that targets only the caster can have that spell affect any other ally within your _spellsurge_ aura instead.

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spell Swipe](/Feats.aspx?ID=2866) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 46

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Requirements**
Your Spellstrike is charged.

</column>

---

You attack in an arc and enact your spell against everyone you hit. Make a Spellstrike, but roll separate Strikes to attack two creatures, each of whom must be within your melee reach and adjacent to each other. If your spell could affect two or more targets, your spell affects whichever foes you hit, not just the first target; otherwise, choose one target to affect with the spell. A Spell Swipe counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after you make both attacks.

 If you're using a weapon that has the [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194) trait, its circumstance bonus applies against both targets. You can use this activity with only melee Strikes, even if you have the [starlit span](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=3) hybrid study or a similar ability.

 If you use [Expansive Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2849) to Spellstrike with an area spell, apply the area as described in Expansive Spellstrike, choosing one of the creatures you Strike to determine the area and whether the spell fails due to a critically failed Strike. If you use Expansive Spellstrike to Spellstrike with a targeted spell, the spell is lost completely only if both Strikes are critical failures.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spell Tinker](/Feats.aspx?ID=5049) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=735" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 205

</column>

---

You’ve learned to alter choices you make when casting spells on yourself. After casting a spell on only yourself that offers several choices of effect (such as resist energy or a polymorph spell that offers several potential forms), you can alter the choice you made when Casting the Spell (for instance, choosing a different type of damage for resist energy).

You can’t use this feat if the benefits of the spell have already been used up or if the effects of the first choice would persist in any way after switching (for instance, if one of the choices was to create a consumable item you already used, or to heal you), or if the feat would create an effect more powerful than that offered by the base spell. The GM is the final arbiter of what Spell Tinker can be applied to.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 122

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
Able to cast spells; Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

Your experience with magic and its traditions lets you specialize in the casting of certain spells, customizing familiar spells to create novel effects. Whenever you gain a feat from this archetype, you either learn to modify the effects of a single spell, or you change one of the modifications from a previous feat. Each time you Cast the Spell corresponding to the feat you chose, you decide whether to cast its normal or modified version. You can only apply one modification to a spell at a time, even if you know more than one modification for that spell. Besides modifications mentioned in the feat, the spell functions as normal.

 Choose up to two 4th-level spell trickster archetype feats for which you meet the spell-casting prerequisite. You gain those feats, ignoring their level prerequisite.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the spell trickster archetype. The two feats you gain from taking the dedication don’t count toward this total.

As a Spellmaster, you are adept at identifying magic. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus when you [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24) with a skill in which you are trained or better. If you have the [Wayfinder Resonance Tinkerer](/Feats.aspx?ID=875) feat, you can change the cantrip you chose for that feat each day during your daily preparations.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Spellmaster archetype.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 102 **Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) --- You can exert your will over magical spells cast in your vicinity, potentially altering or controlling their effects. You accomplish this through the use of a spellshifting conduit, a magical object of your choice that has light Bulk and can be held in one hand. If your conduit is lost or destroyed, you can train yourself to use a new one by spending 10 minutes attuning yourself to it. You gain the Shift Spell action and the Share the Burden spellshift. **Shift Spell** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Requirements** You are within the affected area of an ongoing spell, or you can physically touch an object or creature under the effects of a spell, and you are holding your conduit; **Effect** Choose a spellshift and attempt an [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check against the DC of the spell (or the spell DC of the spellcaster if the spell does not normally have a DC). The caster immediately becomes aware that you’re trying to shift their spell and intuitively knows the potential effects of the shift, but not the result of your skill check. A willing caster can allow you to achieve one degree of success higher than the result of your check. The effects of the check are dependent on the chosen spellshift. Regardless of the result, the spell becomes immune to Shift Spell for 24 hours. **Spellshift—Shift Burden** You share the burden of a spell, allowing you to share control with the caster. If [Sustaining](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) a spell with this spellshift causes a creature to attempt a saving throw, it is attempted against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, make the attack using your Arcana modifier instead of the spell’s normal spell attack modifier. **Critical Success** If the spell is sustainable, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell. For the remainder of the spell’s duration, you can Sustain the spell as though you were the caster.
**Success** If the spell is sustainable, you can Sustain the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell. Spellshifter Dedication leads to... [Analyze Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9356), [Dismantle Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9359), [Elemental Subsitution](/Feats.aspx?ID=9357), [Enhance Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9361), [Reactive Spellshift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9360), [Redirect Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9362), [Subtle Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9358)

fields.text: Feat 2 Spellshifter Dedication Uncommon Archetype Dedication Source Impossible Magic pg. 102 Archetype Spellshifter Prerequisites Trained in Arcana You can exert your will over magical spells cast in your vicinity, potentially altering or controlling their effects. You accomplish this through the use of a spellshifting conduit, a magical object of your choice that has light Bulk and can be held in one hand. If your conduit is lost or destroyed, you can train yourself to use a new one by spending 10 minutes attuning yourself to it. You gain the Shift Spell action and the Share the Burden spellshift. Shift Spell Single Action (concentrate, manipulate) Requirements You are within the affected area of an ongoing spell, or you can physically touch an object or creature under the effects of a spell, and you are holding your conduit; Effect Choose a spellshift and attempt an Arcana check against the DC of the spell (or the spell DC of the spellcaster if the spell does not normally have a DC). The caster immediately becomes aware that you’re trying to shift their spell and intuitively knows the potential effects of the shift, but not the result of your skill check. A willing caster can allow you to achieve one degree of success higher than the result of your check. The effects of the check are dependent on the chosen spellshift. Regardless of the result, the spell becomes immune to Shift Spell for 24 hours. Spellshift—Shift Burden You share the burden of a spell, allowing you to share control with the caster. If Sustaining a spell with this spellshift causes a creature to attempt a saving throw, it is attempted against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, make the attack using your Arcana modifier instead of the spell’s normal spell attack modifier. Critical Success If the spell is sustainable, you can Sustain the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell. For the remainder of the spell’s duration, you can Sustain the spell as though you were the caster. Success If the spell is sustainable, you can Sustain the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell. Spellshifter Dedication leads to... fields.text: Feat 4 Spellstriker Archetype Source Secrets of Magic pg. 75 Archetype Magus Prerequisites Magus Dedication You gain the magus's Spellstrike activity. You can recharge it only as an activity that takes 1 minute. This restriction applies even if you gain another ability that recharges Spellstrike. Action Spellstrike Two Actions Magus Source Secrets of Magic pg. 37 Frequency until recharged (see below) You channel a spell into a punch or sword thrust to deliver a combined attack. You cast a spell that takes 1 or 2 actions to cast and requires either a spell attack roll or a saving throw. You imbue its effects into an attack instead of executing the spell normally. Make a melee Strike with a weapon or unarmed attack. This counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty, but you don’t apply the penalty until after you’ve completed the Spellstrike. The infusion of spell energy grants your Strike the arcane trait, making it magical. If the spell required a spell attack roll, use your Strike’s results to determine the effects of both the Strike and the spell. If it required a save, the target of the Strike rolls its saving throw normally, though if your Strike was a critical failure, the target is unaffected. After you use Spellstrike, you can’t do so again until you recharge your Spellstrike as a single action, which has the concentrate trait. You also recharge your Spellstrike when you cast a conflux spell that takes at least 1 action to cast; casting a focus spell of another type doesn’t recharge your Spellstrike. Spellstrike Specifics Though the base Spellstrike rules cover most spells, various modifications apply to more complicated spells when loaded into your fist, blade, or other attack. One Target : The spell targets only the target of your Strike, even if it normally allows more targets. This includes area spells, which only the target attempts a saving throw against. Any ongoing effects of the area, such as the difficult terrain from scatter scree , affect only the target’s space. Some feats let you affect more creatures. Reach : The coupled spell affects the target using the reach of the weapon or unarmed attack you make your Spellstrike with. For instance, gouging claw would affect a creature beyond the reach of your hand if you used a weapon with reach, and frostbite would affect only a creature in your weapon’s reach, even though the spell’s range is longer. Ancillary Effects : Your spell still has any non-targeted effects that might affect creatures other than the target, as well as any ongoing effects starting from the moment you hit with the Strike. For example, scatter scree would still create difficult terrain in the target’s space (as mentioned above) and tangle vine ’s circumstance penalty would last for its normal duration. The spell takes effect after the Strike deals damage; if the Strike has other special effects, the GM determines whether they happen before or after the spell. Multiple Defenses : Any additional rolls after the initial spell attack still happen normally, such as the Fortitude save attempted by the target of a disintegrate spell. Similarly, a spell that allows you to attack with it again on subsequent rounds would only combine a Strike with its initial attack roll, not with any later ones. Invalid or Immune Target : If the target you hit wouldn't be a valid target for the spell, the spell is still expended but doesn't affect the target. If the target is immune to your attack but not the spell, it can still be affected by the spell. Variable Actions : Some spells have different effects based on the number of actions you spend to cast them. You choose whether to use the effects of the 1- or 2-action version of the spell when you use Spellstrike. A spell has to take exactly 1 or 2 actions; you can't use Spellstrike with a spell that takes a free action, reaction, or 3 or more actions. Spellshape : You typically can’t use spellshape with Spellstrike because spellshape actions require the next action you take to be Cast a Spell, and Spellstrike is a combined activity that doesn’t qualify.

You flare your legs around, using the momentum to both lash out and return to a standing position. You enter talon stance if you weren't in it already, make a spinning talon Strike against an enemy in reach, and then [Stand](/Actions.aspx?ID=2303). You don't take the -2 circumstance penalty for attacking while prone, and your Stand action doesn't trigger reactions. You can spend two actions using Spinning Stand to make two spinning talon Strikes instead of one; these Strikes must be against separate targets.

You trace a spiral in the air while intoning prayers to [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14), gaining her blessing for a time. For 3 rounds, your Strikes and spells deal additional damage against [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), creatures in possession of an imprisoned soul, or creatures you have witnessed create or command undead. You gain a status bonus to damage with your Strikes against these creatures equal to the number of weapon damage dice. Spells you cast from spell slots gain a status bonus to damage against these creatures equal to the level of the spell; this bonus applies only to spells that deal damage and don't have a duration. If your spiral is glowing, you can target a willing creature in its light. If you do, that creature gains the bonuses instead of you.

A hump forms on your back that allows you to attack and trap spirits. Your weapon and unarmed attack Strikes against incorporeal creatures become magical. If they’re already magical, they instead gain the effects of a [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) rune.

**Special** If you have access to this feat but aren’t a bakuwa lizardfolk, your body doesn’t change when you take this feat. You must instead wear a physical coffin, which is a small wooden chest of light Bulk that you specially anoint during your daily preparations. If your chest is missing or destroyed, you lose the benefits of spirit coffin until you’ve replaced and re-anointed it.

You gain the service of a [young animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2114), which has been blessed by the spirits of this world. If you already have an animal companion, your current animal companion becomes blessed by the spirits instead. This animal companion follows all the usual rules for animal companions. You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) to activate your companion’s latent blessing, as long as your animal companion is within 60 feet of you. When you activate this blessing, all damage dealt by your animal companion’s Strikes deal [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, rather than the usual damage those Strikes would deal. This blessing remains active until the beginning of your next turn.

fields.text: Feat 14 Spirit Guide Form Two Actions Archetype Polymorph Source Gatewalkers (Hardcover) pg. 241 Archetype Scions of Domora Frequency once per day Prerequisites Scion of Domora Dedication You fuse with your spirit guide, becoming a hybrid being with enhanced physical and spiritual power. This effect lasts 1 minute; you can end it early as a free action. During this time, you can’t use any other actions granted by this archetype. You gain the following statistics and abilities, regardless of your type of spirit guide. You become incorporeal. You gain resistance 10 to all damage (except force, ghost touch , or spirit; double resistance vs. non-magical). Darkvision. An unarmed melee attack of the same type as your spirit guide (either claws or jaws), which is the only attack you can Strike with. You’re trained with this attack. Your attack modifier is +29 or your normal unarmed attack modifier, whichever is higher. You use the listed statistics for the unarmed attack type: Claws (agile, backstabber, finesse) Single Action , Damage 3d6+5 slashing plus 1d6 force; Jaws (forceful) Single Action Damage 3d10+5 piercing plus 1d6 force.

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 44

</column>

---

You've magically constructed an extradimensional sheath for your weapon that you access through your clothing, typically through a pocket, sleeve, or seam. This sheath is hard to notice, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to your [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Conceal an Item](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) within it. A spirit sheath can hold only one weapon at a time, and the weapon must be 1 Bulk or less.

During a [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755), you can Interact to draw the weapon before you Cast the Spell. You can draw or return a weapon in a spirit sheath as an Interact action, as can anyone else holding or wearing the clothing that contains the sheath. A [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) spell or similar effect can be used against the spirit sheath to expel the weapon. The [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check is made against your spell DC and uses the sheath's counteract level of 1. The weapon is also expelled if you become [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38).

fields.markdown:
May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame **Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78 **Prerequisites** Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) --- You know that when an animal dies, its spirit lingers briefly before moving on. Using low chants, body language that shows respect, and special movements that demonstrate to the spirit that you are an ally, you glean information from a spirit before it departs. This is a 1-minute activity. You must begin the activity while adjacent to the body of an [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) or [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20) that died within the last 1 minute. As part of the activity, you ask one simple question of the spirit. Attempt a Nature check at a DC determined by the GM (normally, this is the [appropriate DC for the level of the animal or beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=554) when it was alive). Regardless of the result of your check, the spirit immediately departs and can't be used for Spirit Speaker again. If the creature had the [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) condition when it died, you can't get a result better than a critical failure. Only one creature can use Spirit Speaker on a given dead animal, as the effort takes the spirit's full attention. **Critical Success** The spirit answers you truthfully. The spirit's answer is likely to be terse or cryptic compared to normal communication with an animal, and it can pertain only to things the creature directly experienced or considered important. The spirit doesn't remember anything that happened more than 1 day ago.
**Success** As critical success, but the spirit doesn't recall anything that happened more than 1 hour ago.
**Failure** The spirit doesn't answer you.
**Critical Failure** The spirit is wracked with misery or bewilderment and gives you an erroneous answer. Skill Feats **Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78 Characters can gain access to the following new skill feats throughout “Broken Tusk Moon.” **All of the Animal**: Head scout Wipa teaches this skill feat to characters who help her butcher an animal for meat, such as the moose at the beginning of the adventure or another animal slain throughout the course of the Broken Tusk following's journey. **Spirit Speaker**: Mammoth Lord Argakoa, also known as Argakoa the Songsinger, might teach a fraction of her tremendous skill to a young scout who joins her in song. **Tame Animal**: The young herd tender Imek has a natural way with animals. She is happy to teach what she knows to any characters who display a similar reverence toward living creatures, such as by peacefully resolving their encounter with the giant porcupine in Chapter 1 of this adventure. Although this feat is particularly useful to characters who want to recruit animal followers throughout the Quest for the Frozen Flame Adventure Path, it isn't strictly necessary for the party to succeed in their adventures. It can be a great boon to parties taking part in other quests, as well. **Related Feats**: [All of the Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=3422), [Tame Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=3424)

Your allied apparitions ward you against the predations of their restless peers. You and allies in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) gain a +2 status bonus to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) checks about [spirits](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=622), and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722). While you’re [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) or [Detecting Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2624) in exploration mode, this bonus also applies to AC and saves against reactions any of you trigger from haunts and spirits. During your first turn in an encounter, you and allies in the aura have resistance equal to half your level against damage dealt by haunts or spirits.

</traits>

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 92

**Archetype** [Spirit Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=274)

**Access**
Tian Xia origin

</column>

---

You’re a warrior who trains your spirit and body to work in perfect harmony, enhancing your attacks with your spiritual energy while fighting with a ferocious martial technique that combines blade and fist. The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6 instead of 1d4, and your fist gains the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait. You don’t take the normal –2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack with your fist or any other unarmed attacks. You gain the Overwhelming Combination action.

**Activate—Overwhelming Combination** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([flourish](/Traits.aspx?ID=606))   **Requirements** You’re wielding a one-handed melee weapon or a melee weapon with the agile or finesse trait; **Effect** Make two [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against a target within your reach, one with the required weapon and one with your fist [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack. If both hit the same target, combine their damage for the purposes of its [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty to each Strike normally.

<title level="2">Spirit Warrior Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cutting Heaven, Crushing Earth](/Feats.aspx?ID=7024), [Flowing Palm Deflection](/Feats.aspx?ID=7025), [Gods' Palm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7028), [Intercepting Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=7031), [Kaiju Defense Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=7021), [Sacred Wilds Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=7022), [Sheltering Pulse](/Feats.aspx?ID=7029), [Spirit of the Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7026), [Sword of Sealing](/Feats.aspx?ID=7032), [Sword-light Wave](/Feats.aspx?ID=7027), [Transcendent Deflection](/Feats.aspx?ID=7030), [Tricksterbane Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=7023)

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />

**Trigger**
You would die. 

</column>

---

Your attuned apparition gathers all of the energy it can through your shared bond and uses that power to disperse itself while channeling the energy back into you, saving your life. You can use Spirit’s Sacrifice even while [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or otherwise unable to act. Choose one apparition you have attuned; you do not die, your [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) condition is reduced to 1 if it would be higher, and you regain a number of Hit Points equal to twice your level. The chosen apparition is dispersed until you can re-attune to it at your next daily preparations.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spirit's Wrath](/Feats.aspx?ID=165) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=15" />
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=135" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 92

**Prerequisites**
[spirit instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You call forth an ephemeral apparition, typically the ghost of an ancestor or a nature spirit, which takes the form of a wisp. The spirit wisp makes a melee wisp rush unarmed attack against an enemy within 120 feet of you. The wisp’s attack modifier is equal to your proficiency bonus for martial weapons plus your Strength modifier plus a +2 item bonus, and it applies the same circumstance and status bonuses and penalties that you have. On a hit, the wisp deals damage equal to 4d8 plus your Constitution modifier. The damage is your choice of negative or positive damage; don’t apply your Rage damage or your weapon specialization damage, but circumstance and status bonuses and penalties that would also affect the wisp’s damage apply. If your wisp’s Strike is a critical hit, the target becomes frightened 1. This attack uses and counts toward your multiple attack penalty as if you were the one attacking.

>
[Spiritual Expansion Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7126) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 24

</column>

---

Your apparitions manifest to scatter the energy of your spell. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that has an area of a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), or [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) and does not have a duration, increase the area of that spell. Add 5 feet to the radius of a burst that normally has a radius of at least 10 feet (a burst with a smaller radius is not affected). Add 5 feet to the length of a cone or line that is normally 15 feet long or smaller, and add 10 feet to the length of a larger cone or line. 

You can also use this feat to increase the radius of an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) spell with a duration by 5 feet by dedicating your primary apparition to maintaining the spellshape; dedicating the apparition to the spell prevents you from using the apparition’s vessel spell, apparition skills, or avatar form for the duration of the modified spell.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lizardfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=760" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Spirit Coffin](/Feats.aspx?ID=6862)

</column>

---

Your spirit coffin can temporarily detain the spirits of those you kill, allowing you to ask them one last question before they pass on. If you kill a creature with a slashing weapon, you can decapitate it and trap the spirit of its head in your spirit coffin. Once before your next daily preparations, you can cast [_talking corpse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1712) as a primal innate spell, which targets the spiritual head trapped in your coffin, not its physical corpse. A ghostly version of the head manifests from the coffin to answer the questions, taking a –2 status penalty to its Will save to resist the spell. After the spell resolves, or 1 day later, the head is released and rejoins its spiritual body. You can trap only one spirit in this way at a time.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Exorcist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171) (Level 8)

</column>

---

You have a vague connection to the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=9) that enables you to notice spirits. While you're exploring but not [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519), the GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) check for you to find [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) that usually require Searching, as well as [spirits](/Traits.aspx?ID=149), creatures on the Ethereal Plane, and beings made entirely of spiritual essence such as [celestials](/Traits.aspx?ID=23), [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=70), and [monitors](/Traits.aspx?ID=111).

 You can also potentially notice [ethereal](/Traits.aspx?ID=63) creatures and spirits inside solid objects, provided they are within 30 feet of you. This applies while Searching, while [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=84), and on the automatic secret check you gain while exploring even if you aren't Searching. You can still notice spirits only on a successful check, and you can't see them if they're more than 5 feet inside an object.

 When you notice a creature with your Spiritual Sense, you also learn its location, making it [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to you if it had been [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39).

You feed excess magical power into your apparition, allowing it to grow ethereal limbs it can use to help shape and focus your spells. This doesn’t allow you to avoid or bypass any other restrictions or limitations normally associated with the spellshape feat.

Your spirit guide enhances your attacks with occult power. Make a Strike with a weapon that has at least one fundamental rune. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. The Strike has the effects of the [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) property rune and deals an additional 2d6 force damage. If your weapon has a [_major striking_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) rune, this Strike instead deals 3d6 force damage.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Splinter Faith](/Feats.aspx?ID=1173) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 8

</column>

---

Your faith in your deity is represented in an extremely unusual way that some might call heretical. When you select this feat, you should detail the fundamental tenets of your splinter faith, though it shouldn’t affect the deity’s edicts or anathema. Choose four domains. These domains must be chosen from among your deity’s domains, your deity’s alternate domains, and up to one domain that isn’t on either list and isn’t anathematic to your deity. Any domain spell you cast from a domain that isn’t on either of your deity’s lists is always heightened to 1 level lower than usual for a focus spell. For the purpose of abilities that depend on your deity’s domains, the four domains you chose are your deity’s domains, and any of your deity’s domains you didn’t choose are now among your deity’s alternate domains.

**Special** Unless you take this feat at 1st level, changing the way you relate to your deity requires retraining, as described in [Changing Faith](/Rules.aspx?ID=803). If you take this feat and previously benefited from any effect that requires a domain your splinter faith doesn’t include, such as a domain spell from [Domain Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=265), you lose that effect.

If you take this feat and previously benefited from any effect that requires a domain your splinter faith doesn't include, such as a domain spell from Domain Initiate, you lose that effect. At the GM's discretion, you can take this feat with other classes or archetypes that gain access to domains through a deity. .

You fragment a ranged spell into a pair of smaller shots. If your next action is to Cast a Spell without a duration that requires an attack roll against a single target and has no effect beyond dealing damage, you roll a single attack roll and compare the result to the AC of two targets within the spell's range. The spell deals only half its usual damage to each target. This counts as one attack for your multiple attack penalty.

</traits>

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 142

---

You can prepare two spells in one slot, giving you the freedom to choose the spell when you cast it. When you prepare your spells for the day, you can choose one spell slot at least 1 level lower than the highest-level spell you can cast and prepare two spells in that slot. When you Cast a Spell from that slot, choose which spell to cast. Once you've chosen, the unused spell dissipates as though you hadn't prepared it at all—for example, it isn't available for use with [Drain Bonded Item](/Actions.aspx?ID=13).

    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Split Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=9078) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 23

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=4260); [twofold tine hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=15)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand, and your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) is charged.

</column>

---

Like knives slicing through magic itself, both your weapons carry your spell, delivering it to separate foes. Make a [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) with a spell that can target at least 2 creatures or that has an area. You can make two melee [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) instead of one, but each must be made with a different weapon and target a different creature. Increase your multiple attack penalty normally after each Strike rather than increasing it for Spellstrike as a whole. If you’re in [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756), you can apply twofold tine’s extra benefit between the two Strikes.

Springing away from one foe, you Strike at another. Stride up to your Speed, but you must end that movement within melee reach of a different enemy. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sprinting Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=9082) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 24

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=4260)

**Requirements**
Your Spellstrike is charged.

</column>

---

Magic propels you across the battlefield as you speed toward your target. Make a [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755), casting a spell that has a [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) area. Before making your [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167), you [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) in a straight line to a distance up to the line’s length; you can move through enemies during this movement, and your movement doesn’t trigger reactions. You can use Sprinting Spellstrike while [Burrowing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

**Special** If you have the [Expansive Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2849) feat, the spell’s area uses the [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) of your movement instead of the normal method of determining the line.

You’ve learned how to analyze and fake your responses to the most common magic used against spies. You can attempt to identify the effect via [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) using the magical tradition skill of the effect or [Espionage Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), even if you didn’t notice the spell being cast.

If you successfully identify the triggering effect, and it would normally fail or have no effect, you can make the caster of the triggering effect think the effect or spell succeeded. If they would obtain a result, such as receive a piece of information, you decide what that result is. If the effect would influence you to take certain actions, you can make it appear as if you were affected and attempt to play along; if the effect normally establishes a mental link, it functions normally, but you can disregard any commands you receive through the link.

<traits>

---

Your enhanced visual gear includes a regulating scope and reflectors, combined in an ingenuous setup that allows you to see around corners within the area of your overwatch field. This permits your overwatch field to extend around a single corner or turn and allows you to see around that corner as well. This ability doesn't let you see through walls or other barriers. You can't use it to see around a second or further corner, and it doesn't allow you to make ranged attacks or perform other actions that require line of effect with your target.

Dexterity 16; Trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1); Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3); trained with at least one of the following weapons: [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=12), [bo staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=17), [halfling sling staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=78), or any weapon in the [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14) or [polearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11) group (referred to in this archetype as “your staff”)

</column>

---

When you [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) while wielding your staff, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to any [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check required and add 5 feet to the distance you can Leap vertically and horizontally. You can [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) even if you don’t have a free hand, provided you are wielding your staff. Finally, when you roll a success on a check to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) while wielding your staff, you get a critical success instead.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the staff acrobat archetype.

<title level="2">Staff Acrobat Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bullying Staff](/Feats.aspx?ID=1194), [Levering Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=1196), [Pivot Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=1198), [Staff Sweep](/Feats.aspx?ID=1195), [Whirlwind Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1197)

May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker **Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane ](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 68 --- At one time, the hero-gods could not tell their own prophecies. Ongalte, hero-god of deicide, defied this rule and cemented why it should be upheld. Those that can reach into the web of fates and pluck out a string are forbidden from speaking of their own myth. Yet nothing forbids them from speaking the myths of others. You peer through the world around you to see the delicate threads connecting others to their fate when they become afflicted. Choose a creature within 30 feet that you can see and who you know is affected by an ongoing affliction that progresses through stages, such as most [diseases](/Rules.aspx?ID=2767) or [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=669). Spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323), then attempt a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) check at [mythic proficiency](/Rules.aspx?ID=3322) against that affliction’s DC. **Critical Success** The next time the afflicted creature attempts a saving throw against the affliction, they automatically gain a critical success. If this results in the affliction coming to an end, you gain 1 Mythic Point.
**Success** The next time the afflicted creature attempts a saving throw against the affliction, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the roll and increase the result of the saving throw by one degree of success.
**Failure** The next time the afflicted creature attempts a saving throw against the affliction, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus.
**Critical Failure** You share the afflicted’s fate, and are exposed to their affliction. You must immediately save against the affliction’s effect.

---

You've trained your megafauna companion to stagger its enemies, impeding their ability to fight back. The attack deals an extra die of weapon damage, and if the attack hits and deals damage, the target is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) until the end of its next turn.

[Stalking Feline Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3438) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

**Archetypes** [Druid](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=6), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=12) (Level 20), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=218) (Level 20)

**Prerequisites**
[Druid Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=701) or [Wizard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=742)

</column>

---

Like Azure Leopard, the Patient Warden, your mask makes you most at home in the night and teaches you how to use the darkness to hunt. You gain [greater darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415). Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell with the [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=143) or [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) trait, you can attempt to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) as a free action. You must still meet the usual requirements of the action you choose, such as having cover or [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) to Hide and being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to Sneak. 

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. For instance, the Cunning Trickster mask could easily be a rodent or a fox, not just a spider.

**Related Feats**: [Cunning Trickster Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3433), [Emancipator's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3434), [Grand Medic's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3435), [Protective Spirit Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3436), [Sky Master Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3437), [Storyteller's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3439), [Thick Hide Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3440), [Tireless Guide's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3441), [Vigilant Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3442)

---

You have completed your initial training in the ways of a stalwart defender. You gain the Tenacious Stance action. 

 **Tenacious Stance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=152)) **Requirements** You are wearing armor; **Effect** You steady yourself, as tough and immutable as stone. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to half your level (minimum 1) and a +2 circumstance bonus to DCs against being [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) and [Tripped](/Actions.aspx?ID=40). However, you no longer negate your armor check penalty or Speed penalty for having a high Strength while in this stance. After you leave Tenacious Stance, you lose any remaining temporary Hit Points from the stance, and you become temporarily immune to gaining temporary Hit Points from Tenacious Stance for 1 minute.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you take two other feats from the stalwart defender archetype.

Your banner makes it harder for your foes to push your allies around and encourages your allies to protect the innocent. Allies benefiting from your Cavalier's Banner feat also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their Fortitude and Reflex DCs against attempts to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41), [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40). >
[Stand Back, I'm a Doctor!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7480) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 95

**Archetype** [Lepidstadt Surgeon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=302)

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42); [Lepidstadt Surgeon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7472)

**Requirements**
You are holding [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727), or you are wearing them and have a hand free; a creature with the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition is in your reach.

</column>

---

You have mastered techniques to aid those at the brink of death, even if they use dangerous Stasian technology. Attempt a Medicine check on the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) creature as you deliver it a powerful shock. The DC is usually a [standard-difficulty DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2627) of a level equal to the target. On a success, the creature’s dying condition is reduced by 1 (or 2 on a critical success); if this reduces the value of the dying condition to 0, the creature regains 2d8+10 Hit Points, its wounded condition doesn’t increase, and it can Stand as a free action. Each creature except you adjacent to the target takes 8d6 electricity damage (basic Reflex save against your class DC or spell DC); instead of attempting this save, a creature can Step as a free action and if they end this movement not adjacent to the target, they take no damage.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[Stand Firm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7368) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=642" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 124

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

Your words help your ally shake off unease and terror. You shout a bolstering comment at an ally within 30 feet of you who has the [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition and can hear you. That ally reduces the value of their frightened condition by 2 (to a minimum of 0). If they are fleeing, they can immediately attempt a new saving throw against the effect that caused the condition. If that save is a failure, but not a critical failure, the ally needs to spend one fewer action on their turn to escape the source of the fleeing condition. This allows that ally to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or [Cast a one-action Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that doesn’t necessarily get them further away from the source, but the ally still has the fleeing condition and can’t [Delay](/Actions.aspx?ID=2294) or [Ready](/Actions.aspx?ID=2299) as usual. If the ally is under an effect that reduces the number of actions they have on their turn, they don’t gain this benefit on a failed saving throw. Once you use Stand Firm on an ally, that ally is immune to it until the beginning of your next turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Standby Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2867) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

</column>

---

You've honed one spell as your favored combat technique, and you've practiced it enough that you no longer need to prepare it to cast it. Choose a spell in your [spellbook](/Equipment.aspx?ID=53) that you could use with Spellstrike and that has a level no higher than the highest-level magus spell slot you have. You can Cast this Spell without having it prepared ahead of time by expending a spell slot of a sufficient level to cast your chosen spell. You can change this spell whenever you add new spells to your spellbook, or by studying your spellbook for 1 hour.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Star Orb](/Feats.aspx?ID=2622) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Kitsune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=341" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 124

</column>

---

Your magic has crystallized into a spherical stone. You gain a [familiar](/Familiars.aspx), except it's a star orb: a Tiny stone of light Bulk. The familiar has no Speeds and must select a Speed familiar ability before it can move, animating in a way appropriate to the chosen Speed and using the statistics of a normal familiar for that day; when it‘s an immobile stone, it can't select any familiar or master abilities that require it to move. It always has the [innate surge](/Familiars.aspx?ID=39) master ability, which counts against your limit for familiar and master abilities.

<title level="2">Star Orb leads to...</title>
[Killing Stone](/Feats.aspx?ID=2628), [Rekindled Light](/Feats.aspx?ID=6880)

    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Starlight Armor](/Feats.aspx?ID=4074) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #187: The Seventh Arch](/Sources.aspx?ID=192) pg. 83

**Archetype** [Oatia Skysage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=199)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Oatia Skysage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4064)

</column>

---

You armor yourself in the light of distant suns, shielding yourself from harm. The armor grants you resistance 7 to piercing, bludgeoning, and slashing damage. The armor also sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) for 20 feet (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet).

 Whenever an adjacent creature attacks you, the attacker must attempt a Will save against your spell DC at the end of its action. On a failure, it becomes [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the end of its next turn. Regardless of the result of the save, the attacker is temporarily immune until the end of its next turn. The dazzling effect has the [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) and [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) traits.

 When you reach 17th level, the resistance increases to 10.

[Starlit Eyes](/Feats.aspx?ID=2856) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 44

**Prerequisites**
[Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756), [starlit span hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

Starlight shines in your sight, enhancing your perception and range. When you make a ranged Strike while in Arcane Cascade stance, you lower the DC of your flat check to target a creature that's [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from you. The DC is reduced to 3 instead of 5 against a concealed creature and to 9 instead of 11 against a hidden one. When you cast [_shooting star_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1042) and target a hidden creature, you don't have to attempt the flat check for targeting a hidden creature with a ranged Strike.

Starlight shines in your sight, enhancing your perception and range. When you make a ranged [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167), you lower the DC of your [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to target a creature that’s [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) from you. The DC is reduced to 4 instead of 5 against a concealed creature and to 10 instead of 11 against a hidden one. If you’re in [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756) stance, you instead reduce the DC to 3 against a concealed creature or 9 against a hidden one. 

In addition, when you cast shooting star and target a hidden creature, you don’t have to attempt the flat check for targeting a hidden creature with a ranged Strike.

**Archetype** [Starlit Sentinel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=275)

</column>

---

You’ve been chosen by one of the constellations of the Tian Xia zodiac. You gain a transformation seal: a mundane-seeming item of light Bulk, such as a ring, brooch, or key, that has the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) trait. If your seal is ever lost or destroyed, you can gain a replacement by spending 1 week of downtime in introspection to reconnect with your constellation. You, and only you, can transform into your sentinel form by Activating the seal.

**Activate—Starlit Transformation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Light swirls around you, transforming your armor, clothing, and a single weapon in your possession into a specific alternate outfit. While your equipment might look dramatically different, it functions as normal. If someone attempts to discern your identity, they must use a [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action to attempt a [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) DC, as if you were using the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) action. Your Deception DC against such attempts is 20 + your proficiency modifier instead of the normal DC. Unlike with Impersonate, you don’t have to attempt a Deception check to interact with someone to conceal your identity—a check happens only if someone else specifically tries to uncover it. You remain in your sentinel form for 10 minutes or until you use Starlit Transformation again to change back to your normal form. 

While you're in sentinel form, your transformed weapon shines with starlight and gains a +1 status bonus to damage rolls with the weapon. You can fling bolts of starlight from your weapon with a Strike action, using your melee attack modifier with the weapon. These bolts deal 1d4 force damage, have a range of 60 feet, are affected by your weapon runes, and have the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) and [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610) traits.

<title level="2">Starlit Sentinel Dedication leads to...</title>
[Blade of the Heart](/Feats.aspx?ID=7036), [Desperate Wish](/Feats.aspx?ID=7037), [Majestic Proclamation](/Feats.aspx?ID=6741), [Sentinel's Orbit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7038), [Special Sentinel Technique](/Feats.aspx?ID=7034)

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Centaur" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=747" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 33

</column>

---

The greatest centaurs need not wait until their stories are over to touch the stars in the sky. You draw an arrow (or other ammunition), whisper a short invocation over it, and then Strike with a ranged weapon. The arrow becomes a bolt of starlight, changing its damage to your choice of force or spirit and granting it the effects of the [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) rune. When the arrow Strikes its target, it unravels into a constellation of starlight that wraps around the target's limbs, imposing a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 2d4 rounds or [immobilizing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) it if the Strike was critical hit. The target can untangle itself by spending an Interact action to break free.

---

Divine glory awaits! You embrace your longing to make a true and lasting difference in the Universe by embarking on the path to apotheosis. You dedicate yourself to this journey, striving to overcome all your imperfections. Each day during your daily preparations, choose a skill you're untrained in. You can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained in that skill, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks with that skill until your next daily preparations. At 8th level, this bonus increases to +2, and at 15th level, this bonus increases to +3.

<title level="2">Starstone Aspirant Dedication leads to...</title>
[Aroden's Innovation](/Feats.aspx?ID=8884), [Cayden's Freedom](/Feats.aspx?ID=8881), [For the Fallen!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8878), [Gather Disciples](/Feats.aspx?ID=8885), [Iomedae's Valor](/Feats.aspx?ID=8882), [Minor Deific Power](/Feats.aspx?ID=8879), [Norgorber's Secret](/Feats.aspx?ID=8880)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 69

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

No distance can stop tanuki from making their way to a good party. You whistle and point, and 808 tanuki, in their raccoon dog forms, somehow appear from the surrounding terrain and fill a 30-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) within 120 feet. The tanuki scurry over the ground, leap through the air, and climb up walls and surfaces, dealing 6d8 bludgeoning damage to all enemies in the area as they’re trampled and danced upon. The tanuki continue to party in the area for the next minute, dealing 3d8 bludgeoning damage to any enemy that ends its turn in the area and transforming the area into [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) (though the tanuki allow you and your allies to pass normally). Creatures in raccoon dog form can attempt to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) within the mass of tanuki. After 1 minute, the tanuki clap 30 times and run off to the next party. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the effect, though if you do, the tanuki grumble as the party ends early.

You've modified your dynamo with Stasian coils, allowing you to make a powerful attack that crackles with electricity. Make a dynamo Strike. On a success, the Strike deals an additional 1d12 electricity damage to the target, as well as 1d4 electricity damage to up to two other foes within 10 feet as sparks leap across the gaps. If you critically fail your dynamo Strike, you take 1d12 electricity damage. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. At 18th level, the additional electricity damage to the target increases to 2d12, and the additional electricity damage to the other foes increases to 2d4. Reduce the operational time of your sterling dynamo by 1 hour.

    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"

[Statue Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6939) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 68

**Prerequisites**
[Teakettle Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6934)

</column>

---

An inconspicuous statue in front of a shop is the perfect form to wait for things to blow over. When you Change Shape, you can assume the form of a statue, shop sign, or other heavy object of up to Large size. Using statue form counts as setting up a disguise for the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) use of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), except that you can Impersonate an object instead of a creature, it gives you a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through your disguise, and you add your level even if you’re untrained. Your weight increases to match the object you’re impersonating while in statue form, allowing you to use your spell DC or your class DC instead of the relevant DC to resist forced movement (usually Fortitude), if they’re higher. You can speak while in statue form, but you can’t attack, cast spells, or move.

Your connection to the earth makes natural uneven surfaces less of a hindrance for you. You can ignore difficult terrain caused by rubble and uneven ground made of stone and earth. The earth has taught you how to remain unyielding and firm. If you roll a success on an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check made to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) on uneven ground composed of earth or rock, you get a critical success instead. This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that would attempt to knock you [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). </title>

<traits>

**Trigger**
Another creature within 30 feet gains the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) or [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition or their doomed or dying condition increases.

</column>

---

As a harbinger of daemonkind, you gain authority to delay the death of others if it serves your purposes, and in doing so, you bolster the well-being of both you and your mount to allow you sow further havoc. The triggering creature reduces their doomed or dying condition by 1. For the next minute, you and your apocalypse mount gain [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 5 as long as you are within 10 feet of each other. If you use this reaction again within that minute, you and your mount’s fast healing increases by 1, but the duration isn’t increased.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Steal Essence](/Feats.aspx?ID=1249) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 73

**Prerequisites**
legendary in [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) or master in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

**Requirements**
A magic item is within your reach.

</column>

---

Being in the presence of the _aeon orbs_ as they deteriorated has taught you how to siphon energy, and you do so with the required magic item. The DC to steal the properties of a magic item is equal to the DC for the item's level or the normal DC to [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68) the item, whichever is higher. The targeted item then becomes temporarily immune for 24 hours. If the object was on a creature, that creature is also temporarily immune (which prevents you from attempting to Steal the Essence of another object on it).

 If you successfully steal the properties of an item, it loses its magical properties for 24 hours and you can move those properties to a non-magical object of the same general kind (such as moving a hat's properties to another piece of headgear or moving a weapon's properties to another weapon) for the same length of time. If the moved properties are [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371), they return immediately to the original item. You automatically fail to Steal the Essence of an [artifact](/Equipment.aspx?Category=45), [cursed item](/Equipment.aspx?Category=49), or similar item.

<title level="2">Capstone Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 72

Characters who have reached 20th level can choose from the following feats, representing the pinnacle of mortal power influenced by their triumphs.

**Related Feats**: [Annihilating Swing](/Feats.aspx?ID=1240), [Astonishing Explosion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1241), [Banishing Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=1242), [Denier of Destruction](/Feats.aspx?ID=1243), [Endurance of the Rooted Tree](/Feats.aspx?ID=1244), [Mimic Protections](/Feats.aspx?ID=1245), [Reclaim Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1246), [Reflecting Riposte](/Feats.aspx?ID=1247), [Ringmaster's Introduction](/Feats.aspx?ID=1248), [Tenacious Blood Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=1250), [Verdant Presence](/Feats.aspx?ID=1251)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Steal for the Depths](/Feats.aspx?ID=8998) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Merfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=227" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 20

**Requirements**
You are swimming in water at least 10 feet deep.

</column>

---

You reach out and grab an adjacent creature (on nearby land or in the water) and pull it below the surface. Attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) the creature. On a success, if the creature is on land, in addition to the normal effects of Grapple, you pull the creature into the water in a space adjacent to you. If the creature is already in the water, on a success, in addition the normal effects of Grapple, you drag the creature 10 feet deeper into the water, moving 10 feet with the creature. Moving a creature into water or deeper into water using Steal for the Depths is [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=2364) for the creature but not for you.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 83

**Prerequisites**
[Mythic Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7287)

</column>

---

You don’t just counter your enemy’s magic, you instantly master it and make it your own. When you successfully counterspell an enemy’s spell using Mythic Counterspell, you can learn that spell as long as it’s on the spell list for your tradition. If you have a spellbook, the spell is instantly scribed into the book, creating new blank pages if needed. If you have a spell repertoire, you can instantly retrain any spell currently in your repertoire to the countered spell, though if the spell you replace is one granted to you by a class feature (such as an animist’s apparition spells or a sorcerer’s bloodline spells), the spell reverts to the one normally granted by that class feature during your next daily preparations.

>
[Steal Magic's Breath](/Feats.aspx?ID=9348) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 97

**Archetype** [Living Nexus](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=392)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Living Nexus Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9338)

**Trigger**
You are the target or within the area of a damaging spell or ability with the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait.

**Requirements**
You are not overflowing.

</column>

---

Your internal nexus has grown to an immense size and can absorb workings of magic even as they form, sometimes even swallowing them entirely. You become overflowing as if you had Absorbed Magic. Additionally, you reduce the amount of damage the triggering spell or ability deals by 6d6 for all creatures targeted by the spell or ability. This reduction is applied before any [weaknesses](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) or [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) are taken into account. If you completely mitigate the damage to a creature, the triggering spell or ability has no effect on them.

The amount of damage reduced increases by 1d6 at 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter.

<traits>

---

When you use [Legendary Thief](/Feats.aspx?ID=809) to steal the impossible, you can steal a prepared spell or spontaneous spell from a foe. The spell is randomly selected from the highest-level spells the foe knows that have a target or area, to a maximum of 8th-level spells; the target loses the appropriate spell slot as if they had cast it themself. You can Cast the Spell once within the next 1d4 rounds, after which the fleeting magic fades; this otherwise works the same as casting a Loaner Spell.

A creature can take damage from Steam Knight only once per round. Your steam armor has the following effects. You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed. When you Leap, you can jump up to your Speed. You don't immediately fall at the end of a jump, provided you Leap again with your next action. If you Leap over a creature and come within 10 feet, that creature takes 2d6 fire damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. At the start of each of your turns, you can emit steam as a free action. It deals 2d6 fire damage to each creature in your kinetic aura with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. A creature that fails is also pushed 5 feet. Level (+5) The fire damage from a jump or blast of steam increases by 1d6.

You transform your fire spells into steam, making them more effective underwater. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with the [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) trait, you can cast it underwater. When you do so, it takes the form of scalding steam. Underwater creatures do not gain the normal fire resistance for being underwater against this spell, but they don't light things on fire or cause [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), nor do they add other effects that would apply to fire but not steam (at the GM's discretion).
